Cavite is composed of several soil types according to soil surveys conducted by the [Bureau of Soils and Water Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Soils_and_Water_Management "Bureau of Soils and Water Management") (BSWM). Classification of soil types in a specific area is a very important consideration in identifying its most fitted land-use. This way, utmost productivity can be achieved.

The lowland area of Cavite is generally composed of Guadalupe clay and clay loam. It is characterized as coarse and granular when dry but sticky and plastic when wet. Its substratum is solid volcanic tuff. These types of soils are suited to lowland rice and corn while those in the upland are suited for orchard and pasture. Guadalupe clay adobes are abundant in the southern part of [Bacoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacoor "Bacoor") and [Imus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imus "Imus") bordering [Dasmariñas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dasmari%C3%B1as "Dasmariñas"). The soil is hard and compact and difficult to cultivate that makes it generally unsuitable for diverse cropping. It is very sticky when wet and granular when dry. Forage grass is advised for this type of soil. Hydrosol and Obando sand are found along Bacoor Bay. The shoreline of [Rosario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosario,_Cavite "Rosario, Cavite"), [Tanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanza "Tanza"), [Naic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naic "Naic") and [Ternate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ternate "Ternate") are lined with Guadalupe sand.

The central area principally consists of Magallanes loam with streaks of Magallanes clay loam of sandy texture. This is recommended for diversified farming such as the cultivation of upland rice, corn, sugarcane, vegetables, coconut, coffee, mangoes and other fruit trees. The steep phase should be forested or planted to root crops. The eastern side of Cavite consists of Carmona clay loam with streaks of Carmona clay loam steep phase and Carmona sandy clay loam. This type of soil is granular with tuffaceous material and concretions. It is hard and compact when dry, sticky and plastic when wet. This type of soil is planted to rice with irrigation or sugarcane without irrigation. Fruit trees such as mango, avocado and citrus are also grown in this type of soil. Guingua fine sandy loam is found along the lower part of Malabon and Alang-ilang River at Noveleta.

The type of soils that dominate the upland areas are Tagaytay loam and Tagaytay sandy loam with mountain soil undifferentiated found on the south-eastern side bordering Laguna province. Also on the southern tip are Magallanes clay and Mountain soil undifferentiated with interlacing of Magallanes clay loam steep phase. The Tagaytay loam contains fine sandy materials, moderately friable, and easy to work on when moist. In an undisturbed condition, it bakes and becomes hard when dry. About one-half of this soil type is devoted to upland rice and upland crops. On the other hand, Tagaytay sandy loam is friable and granular with considerable amount of volcanic sand and underlain by adobe clay. Mountain soil undifferentiated is forested with bamboos found in the sea coast. Cavite also has the Patungan sand characterized by pale gray to almost white sand with substratum of marine conglomerates which are found at Santa Mercedes in Maragondon and in some coastlines of Ternate.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-PNR-49)

### Mineral resources and reserves

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Mineral resources and reserves")]

The greater parts of Cavite are composed of volcanic materials, tuff, cinders, basalt, breccias, agglomerate and interbeddings of shales, and sandstones. The dormant and active volcanoes (Taal) are within these volcanic areas and have been the sources of volcanic materials which form the Tagaytay Cuesta. The drainage systems are deeply entrenched in the tuffs, eroding thin interbedded sandstones and conglomerate rocks which are the sources of little reserves of sand and gravel in the larger stream. Adobe stone quarries also flourish in the tuff areas.

Cavite coastal areas have marl and conglomerate sedimentary rocks and some igneous rocks which are prominent in the high, mountainous regions of western part of the province. Black sands are found in [Kawit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawit "Kawit") while [Noveleta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noveleta "Noveleta") has its own salt products. [Magallanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magallanes,_Cavite "Magallanes, Cavite") has gravel deposits while reserves of sand and gravel materials are found in [Alfonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso "Alfonso"), [Carmona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmona,_Cavite "Carmona, Cavite"), [Gen. Emilio Aguinaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen._Emilio_Aguinaldo "Gen. Emilio Aguinaldo"), [Naic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naic "Naic"), [Ternate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ternate "Ternate"), [Maragondon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maragondon "Maragondon") and [Silang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silang,_Cavite "Silang, Cavite").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-PNR-49)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Climate")]

Cavite belongs to Type 1 climate based on the Climate Map of the Philippines by the [Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Atmospheric,_Geophysical_and_Astronomical_Services_Administration "Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration") (PAGASA). Being a Type 1, Cavite has two pronounced seasons – the dry season, which usually begins in November and ends in April, and the rainy season, which starts in May and ends in October.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-PNR-49) The [Köppen Climate Classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_Climate_Classification "Köppen Climate Classification") sub-type for this climate is "[Am](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate "Tropical monsoon climate")" (Tropical Monsoon Climate).[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-61)

Cavite had a total population of 4,573,884 people in the 2024 census,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-PSA20%E2%80%9304A-60) making it the most populous (if independent cities are excluded from [Cebu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cebu "Cebu")), and the second most densely populated province in the country. The tremendous increase can be observed in the year 1990 when industrialization was introduced in the province. Investors established their businesses in different industrial estates that magnetized people to migrate to Cavite due to job opportunities the province offers. Another factor attributed to the increase of population is the mushrooming of housing subdivisions. Since Cavite is proximate to [Metro Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Manila "Metro Manila"), people working in the metropolitan area choose to live in the province together with their families. Natural increase also contributes to the increase in population. The population density of the province based on the 2020 census was 2,800 inhabitants per square kilometre or 7,300 inhabitants per square mile.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-PSA20%E2%80%9304A-60)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-66)

Among the cities and municipalities in Cavite, the city of [Dasmariñas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dasmari%C3%B1as "Dasmariñas") has the biggest population with 703,141 people while the municipality of [Magallanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magallanes,_Cavite "Magallanes, Cavite") has registered the smallest population with 23,851 people.

Cavite is classified as predominantly urban having 90.69 percent of the population concentrated in the urban areas, while 9.21 percent of the population reside in the rural areas.

#### Christianity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Christianity")]

In line with national statistics, Christianity is the predominant faith in the province, composed of Catholics, Protestants, and other Independent Christian groups. The majority (70%) of the population are [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholicism_in_the_Philippines "Roman Catholicism in the Philippines") under the jurisdiction of the [Diocese of Imus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_Imus "Diocese of Imus"). [Our Lady of Solitude of Porta Vaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Porta_Vaga "Our Lady of Porta Vaga") is the titular patroness of the province.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-67)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-68)

Adherents of the [Philippine Independent Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Independent_Church "Philippine Independent Church"), also known as the Aglipayan Church, under the jurisdiction of the [Diocese of Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_dioceses_of_the_Philippine_Independent_Church "List of dioceses of the Philippine Independent Church") are particularly found in the towns where historically the [Philippine Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Revolution "Philippine Revolution") and [anti-clericalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-clericalist "Anti-clericalist") sentiments are strong.

The [Eastern Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Orthodox_Church "Russian Orthodox Church") presence in Cavite province was a part of the [Philippine Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Orthodox_Church "Philippine Orthodox Church") here in the Philippines under the jurisdiction of the [Patriarchate of Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarch_of_Moscow_and_all_Rus' "Patriarch of Moscow and all Rus'") and its own Orthodox Diocese province in Southeast Asia the [Diocese of the Philippines and Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_the_Philippines_and_Vietnam "Diocese of the Philippines and Vietnam"). Many Orthodox community lives throughout the province especially in the city of [Tagaytay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagaytay "Tagaytay").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-69)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite#cite_note-70)

The [Episcopal Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_Church_in_the_Philippines "Episcopal Church in the Philippines") presence in Cavite province was a part of the [Episcopal Church in the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_Church_in_the_Philippines "Episcopal Church in the Philippines") under the jurisdiction of the Diocese of Central Philippines. **Cavite City**, officially the **City of Cavite** ([Filipino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_language "Filipino language"): _Lungsod ng Kabite_; [Chavacano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chavacano_language "Chavacano language"): _Ciudad de Cavite_) is a [component city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cities_of_the_Philippines#Legal_classification "Cities of the Philippines") in the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"). According to the 2024 census, it has a population of 98,673 people.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-5)

The city was the capital of [Cavite Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite "Cavite") from its establishment in 1614 until the title was transferred to the newly created, more accessible city of [Trece Martires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trece_Martires "Trece Martires") in 1954. Cavite City was originally a small port town, Cavite Puerto, that prospered during the early [Spanish colonial period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Philippines_(1521-1898) "History of the Philippines (1521-1898)"), when it served as the main seaport of Manila. Cavite Puerto hosted the [Manila-Acapulco galleon trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Galleon "Manila Galleon"), along with other large sea-bound ships. Thereafter, San Roque and La Caridad, two formerly independent towns in Cavite province,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-6) were annexed by the city. Today, Cavite City includes the communities of San Antonio (Cañacao and Sangley Point),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-about-7) the southern districts of Santa Cruz and Dalahican, and the outlying islands of the province, such as the historic [Corregidor Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corregidor_Island "Corregidor Island").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

The city has been known by at least two [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language "Tagalog language") names. The first, _Tangway_, was the name given to the area by [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_people "Tagalog people") settlers. _Tangwáy_ means "peninsula." The second is _Kawit_ or "hook," referring to the hook-shaped landform along the coast of [Bacoor Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacoor_Bay "Bacoor Bay"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-about-7) and from which the [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinicization "Sinicization")_Keit_ and [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castilianization "Castilianization")_Cavite_ are derived.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-keit-8)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early history")]

The early inhabitants of Cavite City were the Tagalogs ruled by the Kampilan and the bullhorn of a datu, the tribal form of government.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] According to folklore, the earliest settlers came from [Borneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo "Borneo"), led by Gat Hinigiw and his wife Dayang Kaliwanag, who bore seven children.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Archaeological evidence in the coastal areas shows prehistoric settlements.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Spanish colonial era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spanish colonial era")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Puerto_de_Cavite_1734_Velarde_Map.jpg/250px-Puerto_de_Cavite_1734_Velarde_Map.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Puerto_de_Cavite_1734_Velarde_Map.jpg)

On May 16, 1571, the Spanish [conquistador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador")[Miguel López de Legazpi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_L%C3%B3pez_de_Legazpi "Miguel López de Legazpi") declared the region a royal _encomienda_, or royal [land grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_grant "Land grant").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Spanish colonizers settled in the most populated area (present-day [Kawit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kawit "Kawit")) and called it [Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite "Cavite"). The old _Tangway_ at the tip of the [Cavite Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_Peninsula "Cavite Peninsula"), across Bacoor Bay, was referred to as _Cavite la Punta_, meaning "Point of Cavite" or Cavite Point. Upon discovering that, because of its deep waters, Cavite la Punta was a suitable place for the repair and construction of Spanish [galleons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galleon "Galleon"), the Spanish moved their settlement there and called it _Cavite Nuevo_ (New Cavite) or just _Cavite_. The first settlement was renamed "Cavite Viejo" (and in the early 20th century, regained its former name, Kawit). In 1582, the Spanish founded Cavite City with 65 Spanish households.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-9)

In 1590, the Spaniards fortified Cavite Nuevo/Cavite City with _murallas_ (high thick [curtain walls)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtain_wall_(fortification) "Curtain wall (fortification)") on its western, northern, and eastern sides, while Bacoor Bay remained open to the south. Fort Guadalupe was built at the same time on the eastern tip, and the town became the _Puerto de Cavite_ (Port of Cavite) or _Cavite Puerto_. The [Fort of San Felipe Neri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_San_Felipe_(Cavite) "Fort San Felipe (Cavite)") and the Porta Vaga Gate began construction in 1595 and were completed in 1602. Puerta Vaga (corrupted to Porta Vaga) was the port city's [barbican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbican "Barbican"), the only principal entrance from San Roque in the west. It was flanked by the western wall, protected by two bastions at its northern and southern ends. The wall and gate were also separated from the mainland by a moat, which made the town like an island.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-muog1-10)

Cavite was legally founded in 1614 with Tomás Salazar as the earliest known _gobernadorcillo_ recorded.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-muog1-10) At the same time, the town became the capital of the new politico-military province of Cavite, established also in 1614.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-11) Like some other [provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_the_Philippines "Provinces of the Philippines") during the Spanish era, the province adopted the name of its capital town – e.g., [Bulacan, Bulacan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulacan,_Bulacan "Bulacan, Bulacan") province; [Tayabas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tayabas "Tayabas"), Tayabas (now [Quezon province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quezon_province "Quezon province")); [Tarlac, Tarlac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarlac,_Tarlac "Tarlac, Tarlac") province; and [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila "Manila"), [Manila province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_province "Manila province").

San Roque was founded as a separate town in 1614. In 1663, during the Spanish evacuation of [Ternate, Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ternate,_Indonesia "Ternate, Indonesia"), the 200 families of mixed Mexican-Filipino-Spanish and [Papuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papua_New_Guinea "Papua New Guinea")-Indonesian-Portuguese descent who had ruled over the Christianized [Sultanate of Ternate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultanate_of_Ternate "Sultanate of Ternate"), including their Christian-convert Sultan,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-12) were relocated to the cities of [Ternate (Cavite province)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ternate,_Cavite "Ternate, Cavite"), Ermita, Manila, and San Roque (Cavite province).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-13)

In subsequent years, Latin-American soldiers from [Mexico were deployed at Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_settlement_in_the_Philippines "Mexican settlement in the Philippines"): 70 soldiers in 1636; 89 in 1654; 225 in 1670; and 211 in 1672.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Mexicans-14)

San Roque was later placed under the civil administration of Cavite until it was granted the right to be a separate and independent municipality in 1720. La Caridad, formerly known as _La Estanzuela de San Roque_, separated and was legally founded as a town in 1868. Governor-General José de la Gardana granted the petition of the people led by Don Justo Miranda to make Barrio La Estanzuela an independent town.

By the end of the 1700s, Cavite was the main port of Manila and was a province of 5,724 native families and 859 [Spanish Filipino families](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Filipinos "Spanish Filipinos").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Estadismo1-15):539[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Estadismo2-16):31,54,113 The 1818 Spanish census showed that the port of Cavite alone had 221 native families and 153 Spanish-Filipino families.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Buzeta-17):564

#### City of Churches

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: City of Churches")]

As the town grew, it developed a cosmopolitan reputation, and attracted various [religious orders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_order "Religious order") to set up churches, convents, and hospitals within the confines of the fortified city center. The [Franciscan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franciscan "Franciscan")_Hospital de San José_ (Saint Joseph’s Hospital) was built for sailors and soldiers in 1591. The San Diego de Alcalá Convent was built in 1608, followed by the Convents of _Porta Vaga_ (_La Ermita_), Our Lady of Loreto ([Jesuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesuit "Jesuit")), _San Juan de Dios_ ([Saint John of God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_St_John_of_God "Order of St John of God")), _Santo Domingo_ ([Dominicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Order "Dominican Order")), _Santa Mónica_ ([Recollects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recollects "Recollects")), and _San Pedro_, the port's parish church. The fortified town enclosed eight churches, the Jesuit college of San Ildefonso, public buildings and residences, all meant to serve the needs of its population of natives, soldiers and workers at the port, transients, and passengers aboard galleons.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-muog1-10)

During this period, the city was called _Tierra de Maria Santísima_ (“Land of Mary, Most Holy”) because of local [Marian devotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marian_devotion "Marian devotion").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Squares and parks abounded: _Plaza de Armas_ (across from [Fort San Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_San_Felipe_(Cavite) "Fort San Felipe (Cavite)")), _Plaza de San Pedro_ (across the church), _Plaza Soledad_ (across Porta Vaga), and _Plaza del Reparo_ (bayside).

#### Manila-Acapulco Galleon Trade

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Manila-Acapulco Galleon Trade")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Cavite_City_skyline_1899.jpg/250px-Cavite_City_skyline_1899.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cavite_City_skyline_1899.jpg)

The skyline of the old Port City of Cavite in 1899.

The Port of Cavite _(Puerto de Cavite)_ was linked to the history of world trade. Spanish galleons passed back and forth every July between [Acapulco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco "Acapulco") and Cavite. Galleons and other heavy ocean-going ships were not able to enter the Port of Manila along the [Pasig River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasig_River "Pasig River") because of a sand bar that only allows light vessels to reach the river-port. For this reason, the Port of Cavite was regarded as the Port of Manila,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-18) as the main seaport of the colonial capital.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-galleon-19)

At the height of the [Manila-Acapulco Galleon Trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila-Acapulco_Galleon_Trade "Manila-Acapulco Galleon Trade"), the Port of Cavite was the arrival and departure port of the [Spanish galleons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_galleon "Spanish galleon") that brought many foreign travelers (mostly Spaniards and Latinos) to its shores.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-21) The Port of Cavite was fondly called _Ciudad de Oro Macizo_ ("City of Solid Gold"). The [Wanli Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanli_Emperor "Wanli Emperor") of the [Ming Dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_dynasty "Ming dynasty") once sent an expedition to the place they called _Keit_ (Cavite) to search for gold, received by Governor-General [Pedro Bravo de Acuña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Bravo_de_Acu%C3%B1a "Pedro Bravo de Acuña").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-keit-8) Marilola Pérez, in her 2015 thesis "Cavite Chabacano Philippine Creole Spanish: Description and Typology", describes a large number of Mexicans settling in Cavite and spreading to Luzon, integrating into the local population and leading peasant revolts.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-22) Mexicans were not the only Latin Americans in Cavite, as there were also a fair number of other Latin Americans. One of these was the [Puerto Rican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") Alonso Ramírez, who became a sailor in Cavite, and published an influential early Latin American novel entitled "_Infortunios de Alonso Ramírez_"[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-23)

Between 1609 and 1616 the [galleons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galleon "Galleon")_Espíritu Santo_ and _San Miguel_ were constructed in the shipyard of the port, called the _Astillero de Rivera_ (Rivera Shipyard of Cavite), sometimes spelled as _Ribera_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-galleon-19)

#### San Roque Isthmus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: San Roque Isthmus")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Cavite_City_-_San_Roque_Causeway_in_1899.jpg/250px-Cavite_City_-_San_Roque_Causeway_in_1899.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cavite_City_-_San_Roque_Causeway_in_1899.jpg)

The San Roque causeway connecting Cavite Nuevo to San Roque town (1899)

The narrow San Roque [isthmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isthmus "Isthmus") or [causeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Causeway "Causeway") (now M. Valentino Street) connected Cavite Puerto to San Roque, its only border town. Maps from the 17th century show that this narrow isthmus was once as wide as the town itself.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-24) Problems with rising water and the encroaching waves that plagued Cavite Puerto likely eroded the land into a narrow isthmus.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-muog2-25)

### American Occupation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: American Occupation")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Cavite_1941-10-27.jpg/250px-Cavite_1941-10-27.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cavite_1941-10-27.jpg)

The U.S naval base in 1941 before its destruction in 1945.

Spain turned the port over to the Americans after the [Treaty of Paris of 1898](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_of_1898 "Treaty of Paris of 1898"). At the start of the American era, Cavite Puerto became the seat of the U.S. Naval Forces in the Philippines. It was redesigned to make way for modern ships and armaments. The historical structures, like Fort Guadalupe, were demolished, along with most of [Fort San Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_San_Felipe_(Cavite) "Fort San Felipe (Cavite)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-muog1-10)

Local government administration was reorganized under the _Presidentes municipales_ with the direct supervision of American army officers (the first being Colonel Meade). The first Filipino _Presidentes municipales_ were appointed: Don Zacaria Fortich for Cavite Puerto, Don Francisco Basa for San Roque, and Don Pedro Raqueño Bautista for Caridad.

In 1900, the Caviteños held their first election under the American regime. Each pueblo or town elected local officials _: Presidente municipal_, _Vice-Presidente municipal_ and a _Consejo_ (council) composed of _Consejales_ (councilors). Don Gregorio Basa was elected as the _Presidente Municipal_ of present-day Cavite City.

In 1901, the Philippine Commission approved a municipal code as the organic law of all local governments throughout the country. In its implementation in 1903, the three separate pueblos of Cavite Puerto, San Roque, and La Caridad were merged into one [municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipality "Municipality"), which was called the Municipality of Cavite. By virtue of a legislative act promulgated by the [First Philippine Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Philippine_Assembly "First Philippine Assembly"), Cavite was again made the capital of the province. Subsequently, its territory was enlarged to include the district of San Antonio and the island of [Corregidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corregidor "Corregidor"). The Municipality of Cavite functioned as a civil government whose officials consisted of a Presidente Municipal, a Vice-Presidente Municipal and ten Consejales duly elected by the qualified voters of the [municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipalities_of_the_Philippines "Municipalities of the Philippines").

In 1909, Executive Order No. 124, of Governor-General [W. Cameron Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._Cameron_Forbes "W. Cameron Forbes"), declared the Act No. 1748 annexing [Corregidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corregidor "Corregidor") and the islands of Caballo (Fort Hughes), La Monja, El Fraile (Fort Drum), Santa Amalia, Carabao (Fort Frank) and Limbones, as well as all waters and detached rocks surrounding them, to the Municipality of Cavite.

#### Cityhood

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Cityhood")]

Main article: [Cities of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cities_of_the_Philippines "Cities of the Philippines")

Under the [Philippine Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_the_Philippines "Commonwealth of the Philippines"), Assemblyman Manuel S. Roxas sponsored Commonwealth Act No. 547, elevating Cavite's status to a chartered city. On September 7, 1940, the executive function of the city was vested in a City Mayor appointed by the President of the [Philippine Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_the_Philippines "Commonwealth of the Philippines"). The legislative body of the City of Cavite was vested on a Municipal Board composed of three electives, two appointives, and two ex-officio [councilors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Councilors "Councilors"), with the City Mayor as the presiding officer.

### Japanese occupation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Japanese occupation")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Belfry_of_the_Church_of_Santa_Monica.jpg/250px-Belfry_of_the_Church_of_Santa_Monica.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Belfry_of_the_Church_of_Santa_Monica.jpg)

The Spanish era belfry ruins of the former Augustinian Recollects Church of Santa Monica after the city was heavily bombarded during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") in 1945.

On December 10, 1941, two days after an attack that had destroyed American air defenses at [Clark Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_Field "Clark Field") and three days after the [Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor"), Japanese Imperial Forces destroyed Cavite Naval Base and bombed Cavite City.

Later, after Japan seized the Philippines, Japanese leaders appointed at least two City Mayors of Cavite City.

The island of [Corregidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corregidor "Corregidor") played an important role during the [Japanese invasion of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_invasion_of_the_Philippines "Japanese invasion of the Philippines"). The island was the site of two costly [sieges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege "Siege") and pitched battles—the first in early 1942, and the second in January, 1945—between the [Imperial Japanese Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Army "Imperial Japanese Army") and the [U.S. Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army "U.S. Army"), along with its smaller subsidiary force, the [Philippine Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Army "Philippine Army").

In 1945, during the fight to liberate the country from Japan, the US and Philippine Commonwealth militaries bombarded the Japanese forces stationed in the city, completely destroying the old historic port of Cavite. The old walls and the Porta Vaga Gate were damaged. Most of the structures were destroyed, but some of the church towers remained. The city was littered with bomb craters.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-bomb-26)

After the war, the city's local administration resumed operations. The walls, gates, and ruins of the old city were later removed. Only the bell tower of the Church of Santa Monica of the Augustinian Recollects and the two [bastions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bastion "Bastion") of [Fort San Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_San_Felipe_(Cavite) "Fort San Felipe (Cavite)") remain from the old city.

### Post-war era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Post-war era")]

#### Third Republic (1946-1972)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Third Republic (1946-1972)")]

Republic Act No. 981, passed by the [Congress of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Philippines "Congress of the Philippines") in 1954, transferred the capital of the province from Cavite City to the newly established [Trece Martires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trece_Martires "Trece Martires"). Subsequently, the city charter was amended. By virtue of an amendment to the charter of Cavite City, the City Mayor, City Vice Mayor and eight councilors were elected by popular vote. The first election of city officials in this way was held in 1963.

#### During the Marcos presidency and dictatorship (1965-1986)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: During the Marcos presidency and dictatorship (1965-1986)")]

Main article: [Marcos dictatorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_dictatorship "Marcos dictatorship")

The Philippines' gradual postwar recovery took a turn for the worse in the late 1960s and early 1970s, with the [1969 Philippine balance of payments crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Philippine_balance_of_payments_crisis "1969 Philippine balance of payments crisis") being an early landmark event.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Balbosas1992-27) Economic analysts generally attribute the crisis to the ramp-up on loan-funded government spending to promote [Ferdinand Marcos’ 1969 reelection campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos%E2%80%99_1969_reelection_campaign "Ferdinand Marcos’ 1969 reelection campaign").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Balbosas1992-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Balisacan&Hill2003-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Cororaton1997-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Kessler1989-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Celoza1997-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-32) In September 1972, one year before the expected end of his last constitutionally allowed term as president, president Marcos placed the Philippines under martial law.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-33) This allowed Marcos to remain in power for fourteen more years, during which Cavite endured many social and economic obstacles.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-33)

On February 25, 1972, amidst a spate of assassinations against Cavite government officials, mayor and former congressman Manuel S. Rojas was assassinated by multiple gunmen in the barrio of Panapaan in [Bacoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacoor "Bacoor"), Cavite while on the road with his driver, a policeman, to [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila "Manila"); both Rojas and his driver were unarmed.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-PFP-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-35)

The excesses of the Marcos Family[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-33) prompted opposition from various Filipino citizens despite the risks of arrest and [torture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torture_methods_used_by_the_Marcos_dictatorship "Torture methods used by the Marcos dictatorship")[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-36) Victims of human rights abuses during this period included Cavite City resident and University of the Philippines student leader Emmanuel Alvarez. Alvarez, a descendant of Katipunan General Pascual Alvarez, became one of the _desaparecidos_ of [Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law_under_Ferdinand_Marcos "Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos") when he was accosted by two men believed to be military personnel while commuting from his home in Cavite City on January 6, 1976, and never seen again.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-BantayogFoundationProfileAlvarez-37) He has formally been honored as a hero of Philippine democracy, having had his name etched on the wall of remembrance of the Philippines' [Bantayog ng mga Bayani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantayog_ng_mga_Bayani "Bantayog ng mga Bayani").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-BantayogFoundationProfileAlvarez-37)

During the 1986 snap elections, Marcos won against Corazon Aquino in Region IV (which then included the provinces of MIMAROPA) according to the official COMELEC results, but this was disputed by NAMFREL. An exit poll conducted by American election observers found that voters from Cavite City preferred Aquino over Marcos.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-38)

#### Land reclamation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Land reclamation")]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/62/Samonte_Park_%28San_Roque%2C_Cavite_City%29%282017-04-03%29_1.jpg/250px-Samonte_Park_%28San_Roque%2C_Cavite_City%29%282017-04-03%29_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Samonte_Park_(San_Roque,_Cavite_City)(2017-04-03)_1.jpg)

Samonte Park.

In the latter part of the 1960s and early 1970s, the land adjacent to the San Roque isthmus was [reclaimed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_reclamation "Land reclamation"). The new land is now occupied by the [San Sebastian College – Recoletos de Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Sebastian_College_%E2%80%93_Recoletos_de_Cavite "San Sebastian College – Recoletos de Cavite") and some residential homes. The present Cavite City Hall is built where the north tower of the old western wall once stood, which was already partly reclaimed by 1945.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-bomb-26)

Half of the old port city, including [Fort San Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_San_Felipe_(Cavite) "Fort San Felipe (Cavite)"), is now occupied by [Naval Base Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Base_Cavite "Naval Base Cavite") and is closed to the public. The old historic core of Cavite is now part of the San Roque district, and is referred to today as either Fort San Felipe or Porta Vaga.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-about-7) The former location of the Porta Vaga Gate, the western wall, and its towers is now occupied by the Governor Samonte Park.

### Contemporary era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Contemporary era")]

A portion of [Danilo Atienza Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danilo_Atienza_Air_Base "Danilo Atienza Air Base") was converted into a domestic airport in 2020 called [Sangley Point Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangley_Point_Airport "Sangley Point Airport").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-39) The airport is planned to be converted into an international airport under the national government's Public-Private Partnership (PPP) program. The original proponent status (OPS) contract was initially awarded to a consortium between MacroAsia Corporation and China Communications Construction Company Ltd.,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-40) until it was dropped by the provincial government in 2021.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-41) After another round of bidding, the contract was awarded to the Yuchengco-led Sangley Point International Airport Consortium in 2022.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-42)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Cavite_Boulevard_sketch_by_Burnham.jpg/250px-Cavite_Boulevard_sketch_by_Burnham.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cavite_Boulevard_sketch_by_Burnham.jpg)

Cavite City and peninsula (lower left) in relation to the City of Manila (upper middle).

Cavite City occupies most of the hook-shaped [Cavite Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_Peninsula "Cavite Peninsula") that juts into [Manila Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Bay "Manila Bay"). The peninsula is lined by [Bacoor Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacoor_Bay "Bacoor Bay") to the southeast. The peninsula ends in two tips – Sangley Point and Cavite Point. [Cañacao Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ca%C3%B1acao_Bay "Cañacao Bay") is the body of water formed between the points. Cavite Point was the location of the old historic Port of Cavite. Both Bacoor and Cañacao Bays are inland bays within the larger Manila Bay. The city's only land border is with the Municipality of [Noveleta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noveleta "Noveleta") to the south.

The city is the northernmost settlement in the Province of Cavite, which lies southwest from [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila "Manila") with a direct distance of about 11 kilometers (6.8 mi) but about 35 kilometers (22 mi) overland/by road. Sangley Point, the former location of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States")[Sangley Point Naval Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangley_Point_Naval_Base "Sangley Point Naval Base"), is the northernmost point of the city, peninsula and province. The former American military naval base has since been converted into a [Philippine military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_the_Philippines "Armed Forces of the Philippines") base.

The historic island of [Corregidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corregidor_Island "Corregidor Island"), the adjacent islands and detached rocks of [Caballo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caballo_Island "Caballo Island"), [Carabao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Frank "Fort Frank"), [El Fraile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Drum_(El_Fraile_Island) "Fort Drum (El Fraile Island)") and [La Monja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Monja_Island "La Monja Island") found at the mouth of Manila Bay are part of the city's territorial jurisdiction.

According to the 2024 census, Cavite City has a population of 98,673 people,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-51) with a density of 9,100 inhabitants per square kilometer or 24,000 inhabitants per square mile.

### Religion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Religion")]

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/2016_Official_Portrait_of_Our_Lady_of_Solitude_of_Porta_Vaga.jpg/250px-2016_Official_Portrait_of_Our_Lady_of_Solitude_of_Porta_Vaga.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2016_Official_Portrait_of_Our_Lady_of_Solitude_of_Porta_Vaga.jpg)

[Nuestra Señora de la Soledad de Porta Vaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Porta_Vaga "Our Lady of Porta Vaga"), Patroness of Cavite City.

According to 2000 census data, Christianity is the most prevalent religion in Cavite City, and a majority of Caviteños practice Roman Catholicism. Other Christian religious groups in the city include the [Aglipayan Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aglipayan_Church "Aglipayan Church"), [Iglesia ni Cristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iglesia_ni_Cristo "Iglesia ni Cristo") (INC), [Jehovah's Witnesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jehovah's_Witnesses "Jehovah's Witnesses"), [United Church of Christ in the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Church_of_Christ_in_the_Philippines "United Church of Christ in the Philippines") (UCCP), [Jesus Is Lord Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Is_Lord_Church "Jesus Is Lord Church") (JIL), The [United Methodist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Methodist_Church "United Methodist Church"), [Presbyterian Churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presbyterian_Church "Presbyterian Church"), [Baptists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptists "Baptists") and Bible Fundamental churches, [Seventh-day Adventist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh-day_Adventist_Church "Seventh-day Adventist Church"), [Members Church of God International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Members_Church_of_God_International "Members Church of God International") or [Ang Dating Daan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Dating_Daan "Ang Dating Daan"), [The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter_Day_Saints "The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints"), and other UPC churches. A Muslim minority is also present in the city.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-52)

#### Nuestra Señora de la Soledad de Porta Vaga

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Nuestra Señora de la Soledad de Porta Vaga")]

Main article: [Our Lady of Porta Vaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Porta_Vaga "Our Lady of Porta Vaga")

The [Nuestra Señora de la Soledad de Porta Vaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuestra_Se%C3%B1ora_de_la_Soledad_de_Porta_Vaga "Nuestra Señora de la Soledad de Porta Vaga") (Our Lady of Solitude of Porta Vaga) is viewed as the patroness of Cavite City. She is revered by Catholics as the Celestial Guardian and Protector of the Province of [Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite "Cavite") since her arrival. The image of Our Lady of Porta Vaga is designated as a National Cultural Treasure[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-53) by the National Museum. It is the oldest existing [Marian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Mary "Virgin Mary") painting in the Philippines.

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/70/Porta_Vaga_Church%2C_Cavite_City_in_1899.jpg/250px-Porta_Vaga_Church%2C_Cavite_City_in_1899.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Porta_Vaga_Church,_Cavite_City_in_1899.jpg)

The _Ermita de Porta Vaga_ or Porta Vaga Church, one of the churches in Cavite Puerto, where Our Lady of Solitude was enshrined with the western wall, visible to the left of the building.

The image of the virgin is painted on a canvas. Mary, clothed in black and white like a lady in mourning, kneels as she contemplates the passion of her son. Before her are the crown of thorns and the nails used during the Crucifixion. An inscription was found on the back of the painting – _A doze de Abril 1692 años Juan Oliba puso esta Stma. Ymagen Haqui_, which means, "The sacred image was placed here by Juan Oliba on April 12, 1692". This particular icon was used to bless the galleons sailing between Cavite and Acapulco (Mexico) during formal sending off ceremonies, and was also called the Patroness of the Galleons.

The image was originally enshrined at the _Ermita de Porta Vaga_, a small church adjacent to the Porta Vaga Gate, which was destroyed during World War II. The image is presently enshrined at the San Roque Parish Church, one of the three parishes in the city.

### Languages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Languages")]

[Chavacano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chavacano "Chavacano") is a Spanish-influenced [creole language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creole_language "Creole language") formerly spoken by majority of the people living in the city. Chavacano emerged sometime after the arrival of the first Spaniards and Mexicans in the late 16th century. During this period, the people that lived near the military arsenal in Cavite City communicated with Spaniards and Mexicans and began to incorporate Spanish words into their vernacular. Today, the majority of residents speak [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language "Tagalog language").

Chavacano is generally considered to be dying, with only a fraction of people, mostly elderly, able to speak the language. According to the Filipino professor Alfredo B. German, who wrote a thesis on the grammar of Chavacano, the present conditions do not encourage people to learn the language. There are many likely reasons for the diminishing of Chavacano, such as the influx of Tagalog-speaking migrants and intermarriage.

Filipino writer and poet Jesus Balmori expressed himself in Chavacano, and wrote several verses in it. Don Jaime de Veyra, writer and famous Filipino historian, wrote the following lines: "I am afraid that the inevitable absorption of the 'Tagalog invasion' on one side and the 'invasion of the English' on the other hand, will wipe out or extinguish this inherited Castilian language in existence with its last representatives in the following generation." Professor Gervacio Miranda, who also wrote a book in Chavacano, said in his preface: "My only objective to write this book is to possibly conserve in written form the Chavacano of Cavite for posterity," fearing the extinction of the language.

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Culture")]

### Festivals and events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Festivals and events")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/San_Juan_Bautista_de_Cavite.jpg/250px-San_Juan_Bautista_de_Cavite.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:San_Juan_Bautista_de_Cavite.jpg)

The Original Venerated Image of [San Juan Bautista de Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_the_Baptist "John the Baptist") the true center of the annual Regada Festival.

The city is home to the Annual Cavite City Water Festival or Regada, held from the 17th to the 24th of June. It is a festive and religious celebration of the feast of St. John the Baptist. Regada started in 1996, and features the _Paulan_ or _Basayawan_, which is a street party where celebrators dance under water sprinklers.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-64)

Another celebration is the Feast for Our Lady of Solitude of Porta Vaga, which is annually observed by local Catholics during every second Sunday of November.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-65) The Cavite Fiesta reached its peak of grandeur between 1880 and 1886 under Governor Don Juan Salcedo y Mantilla de los Rios. Postponed in 1882 due to a cholera epidemic, the celebration resumed on January 20–21, 1883, with the governor inviting _principalias_ from across the province. The day began with jubilant church bells and cannon salvos, as town officials, brass bands, and various community leaders paraded in colorful uniforms.

Cavite's streets transformed into a spectacle: vibrant arches, multicolored _banderitas_, and effigies of historical figures adorned every corner. _Calle Real_ glowed with crystal lanterns, while streets leading to the Ermita were lined with temporary stalls selling unique delicacies like _singkamas_ in brown syrup, local sweets, and fruits, alongside Manila ice cream vendors. Households rivaled Christmas spreads with lavish tables featuring Spanish-influenced gastronomical delights such as _paella_, _cocido Madrileno_, and _tamales_.

Afternoons brought civic parades with bamboo _gigantes_ and native games like _juego de toro_ at Plaza de Armas, alongside military exhibitions. The fiesta's pinnacle was the magnificent procession of the _Virgen de la Soledad_. Her route was brightly lit, carpeted, and covered with canvases. Borne on a silver _carroza_ adorned with golden doves and ivory angels, her approach was heralded by the sweet pealing of _campanillas_. The day concluded with fireworks and a reenactment of the Virgin's conversation with the soldier at Porta Vaga. Genoveva Edroza, a Filipino writer, confirmed that Rizal's depiction of the San Diego fiesta in _Noli Me Tangere_ was, in fact, based on Cavite's own grand celebrations.

Other notable holidays include the observance of Julián Felipe's birthday (January 28). Felipe, who composed the Philippine National Anthem, was born and raised in Cavite City.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-67) The city's Charter Day, known locally as simply Cavite City Day, which commemorates the signing of the city charter in 1940, is held every September 7.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-69)

### Cuisine

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Cuisine")]

Food in Cavite City is influenced by its Spanish heritage combined with Filipino tradition. One popular native dish is bacalao (sauteed [codfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cod "Cod")), which is served during the Lenten season. A variation of _[bibingka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bibingka "Bibingka")_ locally known as _bibingkang samala_ can also be found in the city. This delicacy is made of glutinous rice (_malagkit_), coconut milk and sugar.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-70)

## Infrastructure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Infrastructure")]

### Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Transportation")]

Main articles: [Naval Base Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Base_Manila "Naval Base Manila") and [Sangley Point Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangley_Point_Airport "Sangley Point Airport")

The only road connecting Cavite City to the rest of Luzon is the [National Route 62](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N62_highway_(Philippines) "N62 highway (Philippines)"), which begins at P. Burgos Avenue in Caridad district and continues towards Noveleta as the Manila–Cavite Road (not to be confused with [Manila-Cavite Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila%E2%80%93Cavite_Expressway "Manila–Cavite Expressway")).[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-71) A proposal to construct an expressway from Kawit to Cavite City via Bacoor Bay has been raised to the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH). When realized, the expressway would serve as a link to [Manila-Cavite Expressway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila%E2%80%93Cavite_Expressway "Manila–Cavite Expressway") (CAVITEx).[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-73)

Cavite City has one military airbase, [Danilo Atienza Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danilo_Atienza_Air_Base "Danilo Atienza Air Base"),[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-74) located at Sangley Point. The airport is operated by the [Philippine Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Air_Force "Philippine Air Force"). It was formerly a US Naval Base, called [Naval Station Sangley Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Station_Sangley_Point "Naval Station Sangley Point"), until it was turned over to the Philippine government in 1971.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-75) Portions of Danilo Atienza Air Base were converted into [a civilian airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangley_Point_Airport "Sangley Point Airport"), built as a solution to the overcrowding of [Ninoy Aquino International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninoy_Aquino_International_Airport "Ninoy Aquino International Airport").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-77)

As of 2019, no active water-based public transportation services were based in Cavite City.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-78)[Metrostar Ferry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrostar_Ferry "Metrostar Ferry"), which began operations in 2007, used to serve trips from San Roque district to [Pasay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasay "Pasay"), Metro Manila.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-80) A new service from the Intramuros district of Manila to the nearby town of Noveleta to the south debuted in January 2018 and is currently the nearest water-based transport to the city.

## Symbols

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Symbols")]

### Flag

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Flag")]

The flag of the city was created by Mayor Timoteo O. Encarnacion Jr., and was adopted by the [Sangguniang Panlungsod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Council "City Council") through Resolution No. 95-081 dated September 6, 1995, in time for the 55th Cavite City Charter Day. The meaning and significance of the flag components are:

*   The two red strips symbolize courage and bravery.
*   The middle green strip symbolizes progress and advancement
*   The half sun has a twofold meaning. If it is the rising sun, it means hope, dreams, and visions for progress. If it is a setting sun, it stands for the sunset that can be seen from the city's western shores.
*   The five yellow stars symbolize the five districts of Cavite City.
*   The three sets of waves below the half sun, in three colors of navy blue, light blue and white, signify that Cavite City is a peninsula surrounded by water, while the three colors represent Cañacao Bay, Bacoor Bay, and Manila Bay.

### Seal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite_City&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Seal")]

The current seal of the city was designed by Mayor Timoteo O. Encarnacion, Jr. It was adopted by the [Sangguniang Panlungsod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Council "City Council") through Resolution No. 140-90, then approved by the Local Executive on September 7, 1990. On November 3, 1993, the [National Historical Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Historical_Institute "National Historical Institute") and the president, through the [Department of the Interior and Local Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_the_Interior_and_Local_Government "Department of the Interior and Local Government"), issued a Certificate of Registration recognizing the new seal.

The shield stands for bravery and fortitude. The colors red, white, blue, yellow stand for the loyalty of the people to its government. The inclusion of the rays portrays the role of Cavite as one of the original provinces that rose up in arms against Spanish domination in 1896 in the [Philippine Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Revolution "Philippine Revolution").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-about-7)

The white triangle inscribed within the shield with the letters KKK at the corners represents the part played by The city in the organization of the [Katipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katipunan "Katipunan"). Don [Ladislao Diwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladislao_Diwa "Ladislao Diwa") of the city was one of the triumvirate who organized the patriotic group. Many [Katipuneros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katipuneros "Katipuneros") came from the city.

Within the white triangle are symbols representing various events:

*   At the bottom of the triangle is a fort with figures "1872" symbolizing the [Cavite mutiny of 1872](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_mutiny_of_1872 "Cavite mutiny of 1872") at the Cavite Arsenal.
*   At the background is a map of the city including the island of [Corregidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corregidor "Corregidor") representing the role of the island in the city's history.
*   The [obelisk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obelisk "Obelisk") at the left memorializes the [Thirteen Martyrs of Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Martyrs_of_Cavite "Thirteen Martyrs of Cavite") who were executed by the Spaniards on September 12, 1896.
*   The sheet music at the right symbolizes [Julián Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juli%C3%A1n_Felipe "Julián Felipe"), composer of the [Philippine National Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupang_Hinirang "Lupang Hinirang") who was from the city.
*   The fort symbol represents the [Royal Fort of San Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_San_Felipe_(Cavite) "Fort San Felipe (Cavite)") and its role in the city and country's history, being the place where the "thirteen martyrs of Cavite" were detained and where the [Cavite mutiny of 1872](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_mutiny_of_1872 "Cavite mutiny of 1872") took place.
*   The scroll on the uppermost portion of the triangle contains the City motto "Para Dios y Patria" ("For God and Country") in the [Chabacano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chabacano "Chabacano") language to emphasize the native language of the city.
*   The green laurel leaf encircling the right and left portions of the KKK triangle symbolizes victories by reason.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite_City#cite_note-about-7)

The galleon activities also attracted a great number of Mexican men that arrived from the Mexican Pacific coast as ships' crewmembers (Grant 2009: 230). Mexicans were administrators, priests and soldiers (guachinangos or hombres de pueblo) (Bernal 1964: 188) many though, integrated into the peasant society, even becoming tulisanes 'bandits' who in the late 18th century "infested" Cavite and led peasant revolts (Medina 2002: 66). Meanwhile, in the Spanish garrisons, Spanish was used among administrators and priests. Nonetheless, there is not enough historical information on the social role of these men. In fact some of the few references point to a quick integration into the local society: "los hombres del pueblo, los soldados y marinos, anónimos, olvidados, absorbidos en su totalidad por la población Filipina." (Bernal 1964: 188). In addition to the Manila-Acapulco galleon, a complex commercial maritime system circulated European and Asian commodities including slaves. During the 17th century, Portuguese vessels traded with the ports of Manila and Cavite, even after the prohibition of 1644 (Seijas 2008: 21). Crucially, the commercial activities included the smuggling and trade of slaves: "from the Moluccas, and Malacca, and India… with the monsoon winds" carrying "clove spice, cinnamon, and pepper and black slaves, and Kafir [slaves]" (Antonio de Morga cf Seijas 2008: 21)." Though there is no data on the numbers of slaves in Cavite, the numbers in Manila suggest a significant fraction of the population had been brought in as slaves by the Portuguese vessels. By 1621, slaves in Manila numbered 1,970 out of a population of 6,110. This influx of slaves continued until late in the 17th century; according to contemporary cargo records in 1690, 200 slaves departed from Malacca to Manila (Seijas 2008: 21). Different ethnicities were favored for different labor; Africans were brought to work on the agricultural production, and skilled slaves from India served as caulkers and carpenters.

**Cavite** ([Tagalog](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tagalog "Tagalog"): _Kabite_) is a province in the [Calabarzon](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Calabarzon "Calabarzon") region of the island of [Luzon](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Luzon "Luzon") in the [Philippines](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"). It is the most densely populated province in the Philippines. It is home to about 4.6 million people (census,1 July 2024)[![Image 8: "edit wikidata"](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Notification-icon-Wikidata-logo.svg/20px-Notification-icon-Wikidata-logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikivoyage.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q13785#P1082 "edit at Wikidata"). Being near to Metro Manila, its northern areas has become characterized by sprawling residential communities, which are continuing to grow until this day, while its southern highlands become a summer getaway for weekenders.

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Fort_San_Felipe_%28Cavite_Puerto%29.jpg/250px-Fort_San_Felipe_%28Cavite_Puerto%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikivoyage.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/File:Fort_San_Felipe_(Cavite_Puerto).jpg)

Fort San Felipe

Industrial developments are also leading its growing economy, with factories moving to industrial parks scattered in the province. The province is rich with history as one of the provinces which led the Philippine Revolution against the Spaniards. Cavite is the location where the independence of the Philippines was proclaimed, so the province was named the historical capital.

## Regions

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Regions")]

Cavite is divided into 8 cities and 16 municipalities, but for convenience, we divide the province into three possible regions:

*   **Northern Cavite** ([Cavite City](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Cavite_City "Cavite City"), [Kawit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Kawit "Kawit"), [Noveleta](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Noveleta "Noveleta"), [Rosario](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Rosario_(Cavite) "Rosario (Cavite)")) - Coastal communities with a colorful history.
*   **Central Cavite** ([Bacoor](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Bacoor "Bacoor"), [Carmona](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Carmona?action=edit&redlink=1 "Carmona (page does not exist)"), [Dasmariñas](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Dasmari%C3%B1as "Dasmariñas"), [General Mariano Alvarez](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/General_Mariano_Alvarez "General Mariano Alvarez"), [General Trias](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/General_Trias "General Trias"), [Imus](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Imus "Imus"), [Tanza](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tanza "Tanza") and [Trece Martires](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Trece_Martires "Trece Martires")) - A bustling suburban area, with its many problems like traffic jams and uncontrolled development.
*   **Southern Cavite** ([Alfonso](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Alfonso?action=edit&redlink=1 "Alfonso (page does not exist)"), [Amadeo](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Amadeo?action=edit&redlink=1 "Amadeo (page does not exist)"), [General Emilio Aguinaldo](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/General_Emilio_Aguinaldo "General Emilio Aguinaldo"), [Indang](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Indang "Indang"), [Magallanes](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Magallanes_(Cavite) "Magallanes (Cavite)"), [Maragondon](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Ternate_(Cavite) "Ternate (Cavite)"), [Mendez](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Mendez?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mendez (page does not exist)"), [Naic](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Naic "Naic"), [Silang](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Silang "Silang"), [Tagaytay](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tagaytay "Tagaytay") and [Ternate](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Ternate_(Cavite) "Ternate (Cavite)")) - The touristy part of Cavite, with many natural attractions, inland resorts and small towns.

## Understand

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Understand")]

Cavite is known for its rich history and a large number of national heroes, including the first president Emilio Aguinaldo (though some historians dispute this claim). The province is one of the eight provinces that led the [Philippine Revolution](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Philippine_Revolution "Philippine Revolution"), and is a site of many important events during the rebellion. It is sometimes called "Land of the Brave" or the History Capital of the Philippines. Those who live in Cavite are called Caviteños.

They have an exaggerated stereotype of being proud and aggressive people. This originated in the province's agrarian origins in the Spanish period, in which land disputes, peasant revolts, cattle rustling and rampant smuggling along the coast gave rise to the Robin Hood-like _tulisan_ (bandit) phenomenon immortalized in classic Filipino action films, usually starring actors from Cavite’s own Revilla family. Caviteño pride has also been blamed for the legendary feud in the Philippine Revolution between local hero Emilio Aguinaldo and the revolution's founder Andres Bonifacio, culminating in the latter's execution in Cavite. Since the 1970s though, the Caviteño stereotype is gradually disappearing as the expansion of Metro Manila’s urban sprawl has led to a change in economic activity and demographic composition.

Cavite is bordered by Metro Manila in the north, Laguna in the east, Batangas in the south and by South China Sea (or West Philippine Sea, at the wake of the [Spratly Islands](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Spratly_Islands "Spratly Islands") dispute) on the west. Being just south of Metro Manila, Cavite is seeing a rise in suburban development since the 1970s and 1980s, especially residential subdivisions and industrial parks. Bacoor, Imus and Dasmariñas are the three principal cities not far from the boundary with Metro Manila, have become bustling extensions of the vast metropolis in the north, and are bedroom communities for daily commuters who leave to work or study in Metro Manila.
