## Get in

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Get in")]

Common means of transportation from Manila to Cavite by bus and jeepney. It takes an hour or less.

### By car

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: By car")]

One main entry point to Cavite is the Manila-Cavite Expressway (CAVITEX). They also name this road as Coastal Road (name of the road from north end of the road to Bacoor exit) since it is near the coastline of Manila Bay. CAVITEX has two exit points in the province: the Longos Flyover in barangay Talaba in Bacoor and Cavite Exit located at Binakayan Diversion Road and Tirona Highway in barangay Binakayan, Kawit.

Another entry point to Cavite is the South Luzon Expressway (SLEX). Common exit points are Carmona, which leads to Governor's Drive, the main east–west corridor, and [Santa Rosa](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_(Laguna) "Santa Rosa (Laguna)"), which leads to Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, which becomes snagged during weekends and holidays with many travelers heading to Tagaytay. The parallel Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAX), connects [Biñan](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Bi%C3%B1an "Biñan") in Laguna via SLEX Mamplasan Exit with General Trias, with construction ongoing to connect the road with CAVITEX in Kawit.

From Batangas, entry points by road are the gently sloping **Tagaytay-[Nasugbu](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Nasugbu "Nasugbu") Road**, and the winding **Ternate-Nasugbu Road** and **Diokno Highway** from [Lemery](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lemery "Lemery") and **Ligaya Drive** from [Talisay](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Talisay_(Batangas)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Talisay (Batangas) (page does not exist)"), the main gateway to [Taal Volcano](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Taal_Volcano "Taal Volcano").

### By boat

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: By boat")]

**MRS Super Shuttle** operates ferries to [Cavite City](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Cavite_City "Cavite City") from SM Mall of Asia. Since December 2019, there is also a "water jeepney" service between the pier near the CCP Complex in [Pasay](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Pasay "Pasay") and the pier in Cavite City.

### By train

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: By train")]

Construction of the LRT Line 1 (LRT-1) extension to Cavite province is ongoing; it to expected to be operational by 2026. The extension project, will give rise to eight new stations in [Parañaque](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque"), [Las Piñas](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Las_Pi%C3%B1as "Las Piñas") and [Bacoor](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Bacoor "Bacoor"). The line will initially not reach Bacoor itself, but two stations at Bacoor proper are planned.

## Get around

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Get around")]

Much of Cavite, especially the northern urbanized conurbation, is undergoing explosive growth marked by subdivisions, malls, and industrial parks. Most areas of the province are accessible by local public transport, but most new residents in the suburbanized cities prefer buying a car. The major cities in Cavite are plagued by daily traffic jams. Public transport cover well the cities but they are also affected by the congestion.

### By bus or jeepney

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: By bus or jeepney")]

Most locals commute using the ubiquitous jeepneys. You may hail a jeepney from anywhere, though some cities have jeepney only allowed to stop at designated areas per local ordinances. Most jeepney routes run within the province, but there are several routes running toward Metro Manila (Alabang and Baclaran) or Laguna (Santa Rosa or Calamba).

Buses are a more comfortable and spacious alternative for jeepneys, but they only travel on the most prominent destinations. Most bus routes in Cavite run between Manila (Parañaque Integrated Transport Exchange/PITX, Pasay) and Batangas (Nasugbu, Balayan, Calatagan).

The common bus operators in Cavite are as follows, with their routes:

*   Cavite-Batangas Transport Cooperative
*   DLTB (PITX-Nasugbu via Tagaytay or Ternate)
*   Erjohn and Almark
*   Jasper Jean (Fairview-Palapala via EDSA, Navotas-Palapala via EDSA)
*   Kirsteen Transport
*   San Agustin
*   Saulog (PITX-Cavite City/Ternate)

Maragondon and Ternate are only accessible by Bus.

### By minibus

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: By minibus")]

Travel to coastal Cavite may not be complete without taking the colorful custom-made **minibuses** (or "baby buses"), which travel between Bacoor and Naic (with some operating from Baclaran and vice versa via CAVITEX). Cavite minibuses can be basically seen as bus-like versions of the jeepney; fares are cheap and the buses have a separate entrance and exit door, but are cramped and uncomfortable to foreigners. Minibuses were planned to be phased out in the early 2010s (and replaced by the usual jeepneys), but the plan was scrapped after it met opposition from lifetime drivers. Unlike jeepneys, passengers usually give out payment when exiting the vehicle. The minimum fare is P15.

### By car

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: By car")]

Cavite has an immense network of roads, with the Aguinaldo Highway (Rtes 62, 419, and 410), Antero Soriano Highway (Rtes 64 and 402) and Governor's Drive (Rtes 65, 651, 403 and 405) serving as the backbone of the system. Aguinaldo Highway is the most prominent, being a north–south national road serving the largest cities. Governor's Drive is another important highway, from Carmona to Ternate. Antero Soriano Highway is another highway that continues from Manila-Cavite Expressway (CAVITEx) and serves the coastal communities of Kawit, Noveleta, Rosario, Tanza, and Naic.

Cavite has a negative reputation for traffic jams due to uncontrolled suburbanization that created car-dependent sprawl, and it can take 1-2 hours to travel from one side of the province into another. The major highways, notably Aguinaldo Highway between Bacoor and Dasmariñas, are always congested, even in weekends and holidays. The city of Bacoor, from 2016, has implemented a number-coding system in order to reduce congestion, and created a "Friendship Route" modeled after Las Piñas', which is permissive unlike the latter (where a sticker is required). Public transportation is the better choice, but are affected by the congestion. Congestion gradually decreases the further one goes west and south towards Batangas, with the exception of the frequently snarled Tagaytay-Nasugbu route.

The province enforces a road space rationing ("number coding") scheme to reduce traffic volumes on its major highways, including Aguinaldo Highway, Governor's Drive, Molino Boulevard, and Molino-Paliparan Road. The ordinance is implemented M-F 7-10AM and 3-7PM, except national holidays. If you get caught, you driver's license will be confiscated, and receive a ticket and a fine of ₱300.

Cavite's only expressways are the Manila-Cavite Expressway (CAVITEX) in Bacoor and Kawit, and the South Luzon Expressway (SLEX) through Carmona, but the national government is undertaking the construction of new expressways to decongest its major highways. One ongoing project, the Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAX), which will connect CAVITEX in Kawit with SLEX in Biñan, Laguna, has been under construction since 2018; as of 2026, the expressway is open between Biñan and General Trias, and the remainder under construction. Another expressway, the **Cavite-Tagaytay-Nasugbu Expressway**, is proposed to serve Tagaytay, Mendez and Alfonso.

### By tricycle

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: By tricycle")]

Motorized tricycles, or simply tricycles are motorbikes with attached sidecar. Tricycles are a common means of public transportation in the Philippines. These public utility vehicles either have a set route or are for-hire, like taxis. The tricycle is the most popular means of transport for short distances of less than a kilometer in small towns and cities, especially in the rural areas.

## See

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: See")]

While urban sprawl has taken hold in most of Cavite and the primary reason to be in the province is [Tagaytay](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tagaytay "Tagaytay") to see [Taal Volcano](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Taal_Volcano "Taal Volcano") (which is in [Batangas](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Batangas "Batangas") though), there are many places in the provinces still waiting to be discovered.

*   Aguinaldo Shrine.The National Shrine of the Philippines, where the Philippine Declaration of Independence from Spain took place on June 12, 1898. A staple for field-tripping schoolchildren for Metro Manila.(updated Jul 2018|[edit](javascript:))

*   14.214474 120.778334[1](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Cavite#/maplink/24)Malibiclibic Falls,General Emilio Aguinaldo.A Hidden Falls below the grasslands of Cavite. Malibiclibic Falls is a result of a convergence between three rivers flowing from Magallanes, Aguinaldo, and Maragondon. Millions of years of three-river pounding a 100-m high cliff, the water found its way through it; thus creating a waterfall. This river was awarded as the cleanest river during the 2004 National Search for the Clean Inland Bodies of Water – “river category,” in Region IV-A Calabarzon given by Department of Interior and Local Government. The Falls can be accessed by walking through a 1.2-km 4x4 trail from the Maragondon-Aguinaldo national road until you reach a graze land. The entrance to the track is at Barangay Lumipa and 2.64 km before the main Aguinaldo town if you are coming from Maragondon. From the graze land, you need to descend to a slippery soil and moss-covered boulders. The trail down to the falls is not that clear as the falls is seldom accessed by hikers. The trek is about 612 meters and about a hundred meters down.[![Image 51: OSM directions](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/Openstreetmap_logo.svg/20px-Openstreetmap_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikivoyage.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?to=14.214473805547,120.77833390186 "OSM directions")(updated Jul 2018|[edit](javascript:))
*   Pink Sisters Convent,Holy Spirit Drive in Barangay Maitim(in Tagaytay City).It was established through the Society of Divine Word, Holy Spirit Missionary Sisters and Holy Spirit Adoration Sisters, all founded by Saint Arnold Janssen. The nuns’ presence in the chapel gives the place an even more sacred ambiance. A visit is the chance to see nuns praying 24 hours a day — although they can only be seen behind the iron grilles of the altar.(updated Jul 2018|[edit](javascript:))
*   Rare black-sand beaches(Noveleta).(updated Feb 2026|[edit](javascript:))

**Heritage churches** dating from the Spanish era can be found in Bacoor, Cavite City, Dasmariñas, General Trias, Imus, Indang, Kawit, Maragondon, Naic, Rosario, Silang, Tanza and Ternate.

## Do

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Do")]

It's a must for every Cavite visitor to visit [Tagaytay](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tagaytay "Tagaytay"). While on your way to the city, you might want to try the boiled sweet corn along Silang by-pass road. You won't miss the sweet corn being cooked on the large cookie bins which serves as hot pots.

Upon arrival to Tagaytay, enjoy the view of the lake and the volcano.

Would you want to do horseback riding? Drive along the Tagaytay Road and see Picnic Grove and enjoy the picnic park. Avoid visiting during holidays because the park might be really crowded.

## Eat

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Eat")]

*   **Original Digman Halo-Halo** - Digman, along the Streets of H. Rubio and C. Gawaran, is a small barangay in the city of Bacoor. It's known for its famous halo-halo which Caviteños have enjoyed through the years.
*   **Pancit Luglog** is a very saucy, breakfast version of the Pancit Palabok and Pancit Malabon. The primarily difference is in the noodles used in the recipe. Luglog uses a thicker noodle than the traditional bihon of a pancit palabok. The noodle dish is served with an array of seafood garnish, spring onions, hard boiled eggs in thick rice noodles and eaten with local-made Bibingka rice cake. Luglog eateries are located in Rosario and the local favorite is at Rizal and Governor Pugeda Street.

## Drink

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Drink")]

Cavite and neighboring Batangas Province both have a local coffee variant called [Kapeng barako](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Kapeng_barako "Kapeng barako").

## Buy

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Buy")]

There are many malls and chain supermarkets in most of suburbanized Cavite, but national mall chains have begun to spring out in the touristic center of [Tagaytay](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tagaytay "Tagaytay"). Almost all cities and municipalities will have traditional wet and dry market at the downtown. The municipality of [Silang](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Silang "Silang") has a designer outlet mall, the European-themed Acienda, whose main catch is an all-year 70% discount for all stores.

## Sleep

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Sleep")]

Most cities will have at least one or more hotels (especially motels), but the majority are in [Tagaytay](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Tagaytay "Tagaytay"), the main tourist area. At the coast, there will be beach resorts, often the only option of staying there, but there will hardly be one on the bustling northwest region, where the towns grew into the coastline. Even then, the water isn’t that pristine due to chronic pollution in Manila Bay, except in Ternate and Maragondon.

## Stay safe

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Stay safe")]

Weather, crime, and aggressive drivers are major safety concerns when travelling in the province. The weather can become unpredictable in the province during the monsoon season, and roads can become slippery or muddy during short rainstorms. Low-lying northern Cavite is heavily affected by flooding during the rainy season as it is the catch-basin for river systems that originate in the southern highlands, compounded by high tide along Manila Bay.

Since Spanish times, Cavite has had a reputation for warlordism and banditry, which evolved from cattle rustling to smuggling and organized crime, and which resulted in the exaggerated stereotype of Caviteños as _tulisanes_ (bandits). Although urbanization has driven cattle thieves and amphibious smugglers out of business, associations with crime persist mainly due to electoral violence and sparsely-populated parts of the province being used as a dumping ground to dispose of dead bodies.

If you drive, it is advisable to hire a driver, as driving habits tend to become aggressive. The area does show signs of poverty, and common crimes like pickpockets and hold-ups do occur, so be watchful of your valuables. Do not just flash a classy phone or camera anywhere, so you do not attract thieves. Keep them in your bag or hotel safe if possible.

In Tagaytay, beware of tourist scams, especially involving trips to [Taal Volcano](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Taal_Volcano "Taal Volcano") in nearby [Batangas](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Batangas "Batangas"). Always [agree on a price](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Bargaining "Bargaining") when taking tricycles, and avoid drivers posing that they know you: you might get overcharged if you give in. The southernmost parts of Cavite, including Tagaytay are part of an extended 17-kilometer radius danger zone in the event of a severe eruption by volcano. In any case, do not accept offers to travel to Taal Volcano Island in the first place, as it is a permanent danger zone and your chances of escape or rescue from the island should an eruption occur are virtually nil. Tagaytay itself, being located in a highland location, is safe enough to view the volcano erupting, although heavy ashfall can still impact metro Tagaytay. Face masks should be worn to protect against volcanic gases, which are sometimes emitted even when there's no ongoing eruption.

## Respect

[[edit](https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Cavite&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Respect")]

Cavitenos can be sensitive when it comes to local politics, resulting in periodic bouts of electoral violence. Some of the textbook historical figures from Cavite’s revolutionary past have descendants that are still active in politics and society today, so discussions regarding that long-gone period may sometimes be a sensitive subject among residents.

**Palawan** ([/p ə.ˈ l ɑː.w ən/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"), [_pə-LAH-wən_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); Tagalog:[[pɐˈlaː.wan]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Tagalog "Help:IPA/Tagalog"); officially the **Province of Palawan**; [Cuyonon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyonon_language "Cuyonon language"): _Probinsya i'ang Palawan_; [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language "Tagalog language"): _Lalawigan ng Palawan_) is an [archipelagic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelagic "Archipelagic")[province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_the_Philippines "Provinces of the Philippines") of the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines") that is located in the [region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_the_Philippines "Regions of the Philippines") of [Mimaropa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mimaropa "Mimaropa"). It is the largest province in the country in terms of total area, with 14,649.73 km 2 (5,656.29 mi 2). The capital and largest city is [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Princesa "Puerto Princesa") which is geographically grouped with but administered independently from the province. Palawan is known as the Philippines' _Last Frontier_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-UNESCO-3) and as the Philippines' _Best Island_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-travelandleisure-2)

The islands of Palawan stretch between [Mindoro island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindoro "Mindoro") in the northeast and [Borneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo "Borneo") in the southwest. It lies between the [South China Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_China_Sea "South China Sea") and the [Sulu Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulu_Sea "Sulu Sea"). The province is named after its largest island, [Palawan Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_Island "Palawan Island"), measuring 450 kilometers (280 mi) long, and 50 kilometers (31 mi) wide.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-wow-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-encarta-11)

In 2019, it was proposed to divide Palawan into three separate provinces, though the proposal was rejected by the local population in a [2021 plebiscite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Palawan_division_plebiscite "2021 Palawan division plebiscite").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Pre-history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Pre-history")]

Further information: [Palawan (island) §Prehistory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_(island)#Prehistory "Palawan (island)")

The early history of Palawan was determined by a team of researchers led by [Robert Bradford Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Bradford_Fox "Robert Bradford Fox"). They found evidence in the [Tabon Caves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabon_Caves "Tabon Caves") that humans have lived in Palawan for more than 50,000 years. They also found human bone fragments, from an individual known as [Tabon Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabon_Man "Tabon Man"), in the municipality of [Quezon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quezon,_Palawan "Quezon, Palawan"), as well as tools and other artifacts.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-wow-10)

Two articulated [phalanx bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phalanx_bone "Phalanx bone") of a [tiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bornean_tiger#Archaeological_records "Bornean tiger"), besides another phalanx piece, were found amidst an assemblage of other animal bones and stone tools in [Ille Cave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ille_Cave "Ille Cave") near the village of New Ibajay. The other animal fossils were ascribed to [macaques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_long-tailed_macaque "Philippine long-tailed macaque"), [deer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deer "Deer"), [bearded pigs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_bearded_pig "Palawan bearded pig"), small mammals, lizards, snakes and turtles. From the stone tools, besides the evidence for cuts on the bones, and the use of fire, it would appear that early humans had accumulated the bones.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Piper_al2008-12) Additionally, the condition of the tiger subfossils, dated to approximately 12,000 to 9,000 years ago, differed from other fossils in the assemblage, dated to the [Upper Paleolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Paleolithic "Upper Paleolithic"). The tiger subfossils showed longitudinal fracture of the [cortical bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortical_bone "Cortical bone") due to weathering, which suggests that they had [post-mortem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-mortem "Post-mortem") been exposed to light and air. Tiger parts were commonly used as [amulets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amulet "Amulet") in [South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asia "South Asia") and [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia"), so it may be that the tiger parts were imported from elsewhere, as is the case with tiger [canine teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canine_teeth "Canine teeth"), which were found in Ambangan sites dating to the 10th to 12th centuries in [Butuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butuan "Butuan"), [Mindanao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindanao "Mindanao"). On the other hand, the proximity of Borneo and Palawan also makes it likely that the [tiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger "Tiger") had colonized Palawan from Borneo before the Early [Holocene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocene "Holocene").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-VanDerGeer_al_02-2011-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Monks_03-2017-14)

Using the work of Von den Driesch,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Driesch1976-15) all chosen anatomical features of appendicular elements' anatomical features which were chosen, besides molars, were measured to distinguish between [taxa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxon "Taxon") that had close relationships, and see morphometric changes over ages, though not for [pigs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pig "Pig") or deer. For the latter two, [cranial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull "Skull") and [mandibular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandible "Mandible") elements, besides teeth of deer from Ille Cave were compared with samples of the [Philippine brown deer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_deer "Philippine deer") (_Cervus mariannus_), [Calamian hog deer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamian_deer "Calamian deer") (_Axis calamianensis_), and [Visayan spotted deer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visayan_spotted_deer "Visayan spotted deer") (_Cervus alfredi_), and thus two taxa of deer have been identified from the fossils: _[Axis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis\_(genus) "Axis (genus)")_ and _[Cervus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervus "Cervus")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Piper_al2011-16) Remains of pigs were compared with the [Eurasian (_Sus scrofa_)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_boar "Wild boar") and [Palawanese wild boar (_Sus ahoenobarbus_)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_bearded_pig "Palawan bearded pig"). It is known that the Eurasian wild boar was imported as a domesticate to the islands from mainland Southeast Asia to the islands during the Terminal Holocene.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Larson_al2005-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Larson_al2007-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Dobney_al2008-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Cucchi_al2009-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Piper_al2009-21)

Palawan was a major site for the [Maritime Jade Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_Jade_Road?action=edit&redlink=1 "Maritime Jade Road (page does not exist)"), one of the most extensive sea-based trade networks of a single geological material in the prehistoric world, operating for 3,000 years from 2000 BCE to 1000 CE.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-25)[_[not specific enough to verify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early history")]

Palawan is home to several Indigenous groups. The oldest inhabitants are the [Palaw'an](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribes_of_Palawan#Palawano "Tribes of Palawan"), [Batak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batak_(Philippines) "Batak (Philippines)"), [Tagbanwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagbanwa_people "Tagbanwa people"), and [Tau't Bato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tau't_Bato "Tau't Bato") who are from the interiors and highlands of Palawan, as well as the [Calamianes Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamianes_Islands "Calamianes Islands"). They traditionally practice animist _[anito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anito "Anito")_ religions. Palawan's coastlines were also settled by later groups that are now collectively known as "Palaweños". Prior to [Islamization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spread_of_Islam#Terminology "Spread of Islam"), the islands of Palawan, Calamian, and parts of Luzon were under the jurisdiction of the nation [Sandao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandao "Sandao") (in Chinese records, in the 1200s). Sandao was a vassal-state to the more powerful [Ma-i](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma-i "Ma-i") nation in [Mindoro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindoro "Mindoro"). Thereafter, groups including the [Islamized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamized "Islamized")[Molbog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molbog "Molbog") people of southern Palawan (possibly originally from [Sabah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabah "Sabah")), and the [Cuyonon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyonon_people "Cuyonon people") and [Agutaynon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agutaynon_people "Agutaynon people") groups (from the nearby islands of [Cuyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyo_Islands "Cuyo Islands") and [Agutaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agutaya "Agutaya") settled in.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-ptc_history-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-puertoprincesapeople-27)

Palawan was mentioned as "Pulaoan" or "Polaoan" by [Antonio Pigafetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Pigafetta "Antonio Pigafetta") in 1521 during [Magellan's expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magellan's_circumnavigation "Magellan's circumnavigation"). They called it _la terra de missione_ ("the land of promise") due to the fact that they were almost starving by the time they reached the island. The local _[datu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datu "Datu")_ made peace with the expedition through a [blood compact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_compact "Blood compact"). The ships' crews were welcomed to the island with rice cooked in bamboo tubes, rice wine, bananas, pigs, goats, chickens, coconuts, sugarcane, and other supplies. Pigafetta described the inhabitants as being farmers. Their primary weapons were [blowguns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blowgun "Blowgun") with iron tips that could both shoot thick wooden or bamboo [darts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dart_(missile) "Dart (missile)") (some poisoned) and function as spears once their ammunition were exhausted. Pigafetta also described the islanders as keeping [roosters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rooster "Rooster") for [cockfighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockfighting "Cockfighting").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-28)

Before the arrival of the Spanish in the late 15th century, Palawan broke free of the nation of [Ma-i](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma-i "Ma-i") but would be conquered and ruled by the [Bruneian empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruneian_Sultanate_(1368%E2%80%931888) "Bruneian Sultanate (1368–1888)") and their vassals the [Sultanate of Sulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultanate_of_Sulu "Sultanate of Sulu").

### Spanish colonial era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spanish colonial era")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Taytay.JPG/250px-Taytay.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taytay.JPG)

[Taytay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taytay,_Palawan "Taytay, Palawan"), the capital of the Province of Calamianes in 1818 (Spanish Palawan)

The northern [Calamianes Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamian_Group "Calamian Group") were the first to come under Spanish authority, and were later declared a province separate from the Palawan mainland. In the early 17th century, Spanish friars sent out missions in [Cuyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyo,_Palawan "Cuyo, Palawan"), [Agutaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agutaya,_Palawan "Agutaya, Palawan"), [Taytay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taytay,_Palawan "Taytay, Palawan") and [Cagayancillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagayancillo,_Palawan "Cagayancillo, Palawan") but they met resistance from [Moro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_people "Moro people") communities. Before the 18th century, Colonial Authorities began to build churches enclosed by garrisons for protection against Moro raids in the towns of Cuyo, Taytay, [Linapacan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linapacan,_Palawan "Linapacan, Palawan") and [Balabac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balabac,_Palawan "Balabac, Palawan"). In 1749, the [Sultanate of Brunei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultanate_of_Brunei "Sultanate of Brunei") ceded southern Palawan to [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-ptc_history-26) The 1818 Spanish census showed, that when Palawan was then called the "Isla de Paragua" and was under the jurisdiction of the [Calamianes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamianes "Calamianes") islands to the north, the census recorded Palawan island to have had 4,486 native families and 29 Spanish-Filipino families.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Buzeta-29):456

By 1858, the province was divided into two provinces, namely, _Castilla_, covering the northern section with Taytay as capital and _Asturias_ in the southern mainland with [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Princesa "Puerto Princesa") as capital. It was later divided into three districts, _Calamianes_, _Paragua_ and _Balabac_, with Principe Alfonso town as its capital. During the Spanish colonial period, Cuyo became the second capital of Palawan from 1873 to 1903.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] On 6 April 1885, Sultan[Abdul Momin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdul_Momin "Abdul Momin")of Brunei made confirmation of a cession on the island of Palawan to[Alfred Dent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Dent "Alfred Dent")of the British[North Borneo Chartered Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Borneo_Chartered_Company "North Borneo Chartered Company")(NBCC) and partners on the day of 29 December 1877.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-30)A month before, on 7 March 1885, the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire"), Spanish, and [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Empire "German Empire") colonial authorities signed the[Madrid Protocol of 1885](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid_Protocol_of_1885 "Madrid Protocol of 1885"), which established the definite border of Spanish influence in the Mindanao islands and beyond northern Borneo.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-31)

### American colonial era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: American colonial era")]

In 1902, after the [Philippine–American War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine%E2%80%93American_War "Philippine–American War"), the United States established civil rule in northern Palawan, calling it the province of _Paragua_. In 1905, pursuant to Philippine Commission Act No. 1363, the province was reorganized to include the southern portions and renamed _Palawan_, and [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Princesa "Puerto Princesa") declared as its capital.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-ptc_history-26)

Together with [Mindanao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindanao "Mindanao"), Palawan was part of an acquisition proposal in 1910 between then-[United States ambassador to Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_Denmark "United States Ambassador to Denmark")[Maurice Francis Egan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Francis_Egan "Maurice Francis Egan") and several of his Danish friends. Under the proposal, the United States was to trade Mindanao and Palawan to Denmark for [Greenland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenland "Greenland") and the [Danish West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danish_West_Indies "Danish West Indies"), and Denmark could then trade Palawan and Mindanao to [German Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Empire "German Empire") for [Northern Schleswig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Schleswig "Northern Schleswig"), which was then under German rule.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-34) Egan's suggestion faded away when [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") erupted, and Denmark eventually regained Northern Schleswig after the German defeat in [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") following the [1920 Schleswig plebiscites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_Schleswig_plebiscites "1920 Schleswig plebiscites").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-35)

Many reforms and projects were later introduced in the province. Construction of school buildings, promotion of agriculture, and bringing people closer to the government were among the priority plans during this era.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-ptc_history-26)

### Japanese invasion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Japanese invasion")]

After the Japanese invasion, according to Stephen L. Moore, "Pro-Allied sentiment was strong, and it was later estimated that during the war as many as 1,154 Filipino guerrillas worked against the Japanese on the island. Those in the underground network would proudly refer to themselves as 'Palawan's Fighting One Thousand'." Early resistance leaders included Dr. Higinio Acosta Mendoza, his wife Triny, Thomas F. Loudon, and his son-in-law Nazario Mayor. Capt. Mayor organized Company D in October 1943, and was responsible for the area encompassing Puerto Princesa south to [Balabac Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balabac_Island "Balabac Island"). Capt. Mendoza covered the area north of Puerto Princesa to Caramay. Lt. Felipe Batul operated out of Danlig, while Capt. Carlos Amores operated out of Sibaltan. Overall command of the Palawan Special Battalion was under Major Pablo P. Muyco as part of the 6th [Military District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_District "Military District"). The Palawan guerrillas helped any escaping American POWs, supported two [coastwatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastwatcher "Coastwatcher") groups sending regular radio broadcasts to [General MacArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_MacArthur "General MacArthur") on Japanese movements, and helped rescue downed airmen as well as survivors from the submarine [USS _Flier_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Flier "USS Flier"). Most importantly, they helped guide the [8th Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8th_Army_(United_States) "8th Army (United States)")'s troop landings.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Moore-36)

#### Palawan Massacre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Palawan Massacre")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/BurnedAtBaatan.gif/250px-BurnedAtBaatan.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BurnedAtBaatan.gif)

U.S. Army personnel worked to identify the charred remains of Americans captured at [Bataan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bataan "Bataan") and burned alive on Palawan. March 20, 1945

Main article: [Palawan Massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_Massacre "Palawan Massacre")

During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), in order to prevent the rescue of [prisoners of war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoners_of_war "Prisoners of war") by the advancing allies, on December 14, 1944, units of the [Japanese Fourteenth Area Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Fourteenth_Area_Army "Japanese Fourteenth Area Army") (under the command of General [Tomoyuki Yamashita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomoyuki_Yamashita "Tomoyuki Yamashita")) herded the remaining 150 prisoners of war at [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Princesa "Puerto Princesa") into three covered trenches which were then set on fire using barrels of gasoline. Prisoners who tried to escape the flames were shot down.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-37) Only 11 men escaped the slaughter.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Bob-38)

#### Liberation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Liberation")]

Main article: [Invasion of Palawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Palawan "Invasion of Palawan")

During the first phase of the [Battle of Leyte Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Leyte_Gulf "Battle of Leyte Gulf"), just off the coast of Palawan, two [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") submarines, [USS _Dace_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Dace_(SS-247) "USS Dace (SS-247)") and [USS _Darter_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Darter_(SS-227) "USS Darter (SS-227)") attacked a Japanese cruiser task force led by Admiral [Takeo Kurita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takeo_Kurita "Takeo Kurita"), sinking his flagship (in which he survived) [_Atago_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_cruiser_Atago "Japanese cruiser Atago"), and her sister ship [_Maya_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_cruiser_Maya "Japanese cruiser Maya"). _Darter_ later ran aground that afternoon and was scuttled by [USS _Nautilus_(SS-168)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Nautilus_(SS-168) "USS Nautilus (SS-168)").

The island was liberated from the Japanese Imperial Forces from February 28 to April 22, 1945, during the [Invasion of Palawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Palawan "Invasion of Palawan").

### Martial law era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Martial law era")]

Like the other parts of the Philippines, Palawan felt the impact when [Ferdinand Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos "Ferdinand Marcos") placed the whole country under martial law in September 1972, and then held on to power for 14 more years, until he was ousted by the 1986 EDSA [People Power revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_Power_revolution "People Power revolution").

One incident was when Marcos evicted an estimated 254 families of Indigenous [Tagbanwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagbanwa "Tagbanwa") people from the [Calauit Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calauit_Island "Calauit Island") in order to create a game reserve full of animals imported from Africa.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-:0b-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-40)

In another incident, residents of [Bugsuk Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugsuk_Island "Bugsuk Island") were driven from their homes and communities so that Marcos' crony [Eduardo Cojuangco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Cojuangco "Eduardo Cojuangco") could establish a coconut plantation.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-BantayogProfileOsorio-41)

Among the leaders who helped organize the effort to prevent the eviction of the Bugsuk Island residents was [United Methodist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Methodist_Church "United Methodist Church") Reverend [Magnifico Osorio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnifico_Osorio "Magnifico Osorio"). When the effort failed, Reverend Osorio relocated to [Bataraza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bataraza "Bataraza"), a town on the southernmost tip of Palawan Island, where he continued to fight for the rights of the Indigenous peoples of Palawan. In March 1985 he successfully facilitated a meeting between Indigenous peoples and the provincial governor at that time Salvador Paredes Socrates, who promised to respect Indigenous rights as long as he was governor. A few weeks later, however, Reverend Osorio was found dead out in his ricefields, having been clubbed in the head and shot dead. For his work to protect the Indigenous peoples of Palawan, and for the circumstances of his death, Reverend Osorio was honored by having his name inscribed on the Wall of Remembrance at the Philippines' [Bantayog ng mga Bayani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantayog_ng_mga_Bayani "Bantayog ng mga Bayani"), which honors the martyrs and heroes who fought the [abuses of the Marcos dictatorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abuses_of_the_Marcos_dictatorship "Abuses of the Marcos dictatorship").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-BantayogProfileOsorio-41)

The Marcos era was [a time of significant deforestation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deforestation_in_the_Philippines#Deforestation_during_the_martial_law_era "Deforestation in the Philippines") in Palawan and throughout the Philippines, with the forest cover of the Philippines shrinking until only 8% remained.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Dixon2010-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Inoue2013-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-nhcp3-44) In Palawan, one major company given a Timber License Agreements (TLA) to cut down trees during Martial Law was Palawan-Apitong Corp, which was owned by [Juan Ponce Enrile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Ponce_Enrile "Juan Ponce Enrile").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-nhcp3-44) Enrile was the government official Ferdinand Marcos put in place to approve Timber License Agreements during Martial Law.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-nhcp3-44)

### Contemporary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Contemporary")]

In 2005, Palawan was briefly made politically part of [Western Visayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Visayas "Western Visayas") or _Region VI_ through Executive Order 429 signed by then-President [Gloria Macapagal Arroyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Macapagal_Arroyo "Gloria Macapagal Arroyo") on May 23[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-46) as a political move to control the province and a response to getting more loans from [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] This decree was later deferred on August 18 within the same year reportedly due to the opposition of the province's [Sangguniang Panlalawigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangguniang_Panlalawigan "Sangguniang Panlalawigan") (Provincial Council).[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-47)

On July 21, 2007, its capital city [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Princesa "Puerto Princesa") became a [highly urbanized city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cities_of_the_Philippines#Legal_classification "Cities of the Philippines").

In April 2019, a bill dividing Palawan into three provinces was passed into law.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-MB-MoveAssailed-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-PIAGovPH-DividesPalawan-49) The proposed three new provinces were Palawan del Norte, Palawan Oriental, and Palawan del Sur.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-:0-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-:1-51) Some civil society groups and Puerto Princesa residents opposed the proposed division, claiming that there was no extensive public consultation.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-MB-MoveAssailed-48)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-ABSCBNNews-DividingPalawan-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-GMANews-SplittingPalawan-54) The [Comelec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_(Philippines) "Commission on Elections (Philippines)") announced on March 16, 2021, that the majority of Palawan residents opposed the division in the [plebiscite held on March 13, 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Palawan_division_plebiscite "2021 Palawan division plebiscite").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-cnnphilippines.com-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-rappler.com-56)

Local Palaweño officials on January 6, 2026 opposed Palawan's inclusion in [Mindanao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindanao "Mindanao"), in response to a resolution by some figures in [Cagayan de Oro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagayan_de_Oro "Cagayan de Oro") referencing "Minsupala" union (Mindanao–Sulu–Palawan) should the island group [secede from the rest of the country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Separatism_in_the_Philippines "Separatism in the Philippines"). They denounced the inclusion of the province in a map that the said personalities planned to submit to the United Nations [Special Committee on Decolonization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Committee_on_Decolonization "Special Committee on Decolonization"). Board member Ryan Maminta asserted that "Minsupala" was never a political and legal entity, rather it was only an anthropological term "illustrating the connections and trade routes during the pre-colonial period".[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-57)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Coron_island_-_Straight_out_of_a_dream.jpg/250px-Coron_island_-_Straight_out_of_a_dream.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Coron_island_-_Straight_out_of_a_dream.jpg)

Coron Island

The province is composed of the long and narrow [Palawan Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_Island "Palawan Island"), plus a number of other smaller islands surrounding it, totalling roughly 1,780 islands and islets. The [Calamianes Group of Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamian_Islands "Calamian Islands") to the northeast consists of [Busuanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busuanga_Island "Busuanga Island"), [Coron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coron_Island "Coron Island"), [Culion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culion "Culion"), and [Linapacan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linapacan "Linapacan") islands. [Balabac Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balabac_Island "Balabac Island") is located off the southern tip, separated from [Borneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo "Borneo") by the [Balabac Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balabac_Strait "Balabac Strait"). In addition, Palawan covers the [Cuyo Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyo_Islands "Cuyo Islands") in the [Sulu Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulu_Sea "Sulu Sea"). The disputed [Spratly Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spratly_Islands "Spratly Islands"), located a few hundred kilometers to the west, are considered part of Palawan by the Philippines, and is locally called the "Kalayaan Group of Islands".

Palawan's almost 2,000 kilometers (1,200 mi) of irregular coastline is lined with rocky coves and sugar-white sandy beaches. It also harbors a vast stretch of virgin forests that carpet its chain of mountain ranges. The mountain heights average 1,100 meters (3,500 ft) in altitude, with the highest peak rising to 6,843 feet (2,086 m)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-encarta-11) at [Mount Mantalingahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Mantalingahan "Mount Mantalingahan"). The vast mountain areas are the source of valuable timber. The terrain is a mix of coastal plain, craggy foothills, valley deltas, and heavy forest interspersed with riverine arteries that serve as irrigation.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-wow-10)

The province has a total land area of 14,649.73 square kilometers (5,656.29 sq mi).[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-nscb-58) When [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Princesa "Puerto Princesa") City is included for geographical purposes, its land area is 17,030.75 square kilometers (6,575.61 sq mi).[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-nscb-58) The land area is distributed to its _mainland municipalities_, comprising 12,239 square kilometers (4,726 sq mi), and the _island municipalities_, which altogether measure 2,657 square kilometers (1,026 sq mi). In terms of archipelagic internal waters, Palawan has the biggest marine resources that covers almost half of the Sulu Sea and a big chunk of the South China Sea that is within the municipal waters of Kalayaan Municipality which was officially annexed to the Philippine jurisdiction by virtue of _Presidential Decree 1596_ dated June 11,1978.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Climate")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Palawan%2C_Tropical_jungle_rainforest.jpg/250px-Palawan%2C_Tropical_jungle_rainforest.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Palawan,_Tropical_jungle_rainforest.jpg)

Primary tropical moist rainforest in central Palawan

The province has two types of climate. The first, which occurs in the northern and southern extremities and the entire western coast, has two distinct seasons – eight months dry and seven months wet. The other, which prevails in the eastern coast, has a short dry season of one to three months and no pronounced rainy period during the rest of the year. The southern part of the province is virtually free from tropical depressions but northern Palawan experiences torrential rains during the months of July and August. Summer months serve as peak season for Palawan. Sea voyages are most favorable from March to early June when the seas are calm. The average maximum temperature is 31°C (88°F) with largre variation all year.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-wow-10)

The land ecosystem of Palawan is threatened by [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-60) For example, though mangroves and barrier reefs protect Puerto Princesa's coastlines from [supertyphoons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon "Typhoon"), these barriers are subject to degradation due to [El Niño](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Ni%C3%B1o "El Niño"), rising sea temperatures, and other climate change-related phenomena.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-61) A study by the [World Wide Fund for Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Fund_for_Nature "World Wide Fund for Nature") revealed that a spike in ocean acidification in 2010 came from Palawan's waters.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-62)

### Administrative divisions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Administrative divisions")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Ph_fil_palawan.png/960px-Ph_fil_palawan.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ph_fil_palawan.png)

Political map of Palawan

Palawan comprises 433 [barangays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barangays "Barangays") in 23 municipalities and the capital City of Puerto Princesa. As an archipelago, Palawan has 13 [mainland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_(island) "Palawan (island)") municipalities and 10 island towns. There are three [congressional districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislative_districts_of_Palawan "Legislative districts of Palawan"), namely: the first district comprising five northern mainland municipalities and nine island towns; the second district composed of six southern mainland towns and the island municipality of Balabac; and the third district covering the capital City of Puerto Princesa and the town of Aborlan. Thirteen municipalities are considered as _mainland municipalities_, namely [Aborlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aborlan "Aborlan"), [Narra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narra,_Palawan "Narra, Palawan"), [Quezon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quezon,_Palawan "Quezon, Palawan"), [Sofronio Española](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sofronio_Espa%C3%B1ola,_Palawan "Sofronio Española, Palawan"), [Brooke's Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooke's_Point,_Palawan "Brooke's Point, Palawan"), [Rizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rizal,_Palawan "Rizal, Palawan"), and [Bataraza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bataraza "Bataraza") (located south); [San Vicente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Vicente,_Palawan "San Vicente, Palawan"), [Roxas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxas,_Palawan "Roxas, Palawan"), [Dumaran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dumaran "Dumaran"), [El Nido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Nido,_Palawan "El Nido, Palawan"), and [Taytay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taytay,_Palawan "Taytay, Palawan") (found in the north). The remaining _island municipalities_ are: [Busuanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busuanga "Busuanga"), [Coron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coron,_Palawan "Coron, Palawan"), [Linapacan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linapacan "Linapacan") and [Culion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culion "Culion") (forming the [Calamianes group of islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamian_Group "Calamian Group")), [Cuyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyo,_Palawan "Cuyo, Palawan"), [Agutaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agutaya "Agutaya") and [Magsaysay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magsaysay,_Palawan "Magsaysay, Palawan") (the [Cuyo group of islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyo,_Palawan "Cuyo, Palawan")), [Araceli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Araceli,_Palawan "Araceli, Palawan"), [Cagayancillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagayancillo "Cagayancillo"), [Balabac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balabac "Balabac") and [Kalayaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalayaan,_Palawan "Kalayaan, Palawan") ([Spratly Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spratly_Islands "Spratly Islands")). The capital, [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Princesa "Puerto Princesa") is a [highly urbanized city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cities_of_the_Philippines#Independent_cities "Cities of the Philippines") that governs itself independently from the province, but it usually grouped with the province for statistical and geographic purposes.

### Proposals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Proposals")]

#### Inclusion into other regions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Inclusion into other regions")]

In 2001, the residents of Palawan voted in a [plebiscite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plebiscite "Plebiscite") to reject inclusion into an expanded [Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_Region_in_Muslim_Mindanao "Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-65)

On May 17, 2002, _Executive Order No. 103_ divided _[Region IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern\_Tagalog "Southern Tagalog")_ into _Region IV-A_ ([Calabarzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabarzon "Calabarzon")) and _Region IV-B_ ([Mimaropa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mimaropa "Mimaropa")), placing the province of Palawan into Mimaropa.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-EO103-66)

On May 23, 2005, _Executive Order No. 429_ directed that Palawan be transferred from _Region IV-B_ to [Region VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Visayas "Western Visayas").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-EO429-5) However, Palaweños criticized the move, citing a lack of consultation, with most residents in Puerto Princesa City and all municipalities but one preferring to stay with Region IV-B. Consequently, _Administrative Order No. 129_ was issued on August 19, 2005, that the implementation of _EO 429_ be held in [abeyance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abeyance "Abeyance") pending approval by the President of its implementation Plan.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-AO129-6) The Philippine [Commission on Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_(Philippines) "Commission on Elections (Philippines)") reported the [2010 Philippine general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Philippine_general_election "2010 Philippine general election") results for Palawan as a part of the Region IV-B results.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-67)As of 30 June 2011[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit), the abeyance was still in effect and Palawan remained a part of [Mimaropa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mimaropa "Mimaropa").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-nscblist-7)

#### Proposed division into three provinces

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Proposed division into three provinces")]

Main article: [2021 Palawan division plebiscite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Palawan_division_plebiscite "2021 Palawan division plebiscite")

A March 2021 plebiscite (originally scheduled for May 2020 but delayed due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic")[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Palawan_News_Online-68)) asked about whether to divided Palawan into three provinces:[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-70) Palawan del Norte (including El Nido, Taytay, Coron, Linapacan, Culion, and Busuanga), Palawan Oriental (includes San Vicente, Roxas, Dumaran, Cuyo, Agutaya, Magsaysay, and Cagayancillo), and Palawan del Sur (includes Kalayaan, Aborlan, Narra, Sofronio Española, Brooke's Point, Rizal, Quezon, Bataraza and Balabac).[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-:0-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-:1-51) The division was rejected by a majority.

### Religion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Palawan&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Religion")]

Main article: [Religion in the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religion_in_the_Philippines "Religion in the Philippines")

Religiously, the drastic increase in [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") is related to the increase in the number of migrants, especially those from [Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzon "Luzon"), who are increasingly coming to Palawan. In 2000, [Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam "Islam") in Palawan was 23.6%, a percentage that decreased drastically in 2020 to 10.83%, along with the arrival of Christian settlers. Previously, almost half of the population in Palawan was [Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims"), almost all of them indigenous people, especially [Molbog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molbog_people "Molbog people") and [Southern Palawano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawano_people "Palawano people").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-74)

#### Roman Catholicism

Main articles: [Apostolic Vicariate of Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Vicariate_of_Puerto_Princesa "Apostolic Vicariate of Puerto Princesa") and [Apostolic Vicariate of Taytay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Vicariate_of_Taytay "Apostolic Vicariate of Taytay")

The predominant religion in Palawan is [Roman Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholicism "Roman Catholicism"). In 2017, the Roman Catholic Apostolic Vicariate of Puerto Princesa had a 68.8% adherence while the Roman Catholic Apostolic Vicariate of Taytay (Northern Palawan) had a 91.6% adherence.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-gcatholic.org-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-ReferenceA-76) One of the [religious orders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_order "Religious order") that had a significant mission in the islands is the [Order of Augustinian Recollects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Augustinian_Recollects "Order of Augustinian Recollects").

The Catholics in the province are governed by a single [apostolic vicariate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_vicariate "Apostolic vicariate") until 2002 when it was divided into two: the Apostolic Vicariate of [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Vicariate_of_Puerto_Princesa "Apostolic Vicariate of Puerto Princesa") in Southern Palawan and the Apostolic Vicariate of [Taytay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Vicariate_of_Taytay "Apostolic Vicariate of Taytay") in Northern Palawan.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-ReferenceA-76)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-gcatholic.org-75)

#### Protestantism and other groups

Several [Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist "Baptist") and other Protestant denominations have a strong presence in Palawan as do the [Church of the Foursquare Gospel in the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_the_Foursquare_Gospel_in_the_Philippines "Church of the Foursquare Gospel in the Philippines"), and the [Seventh-day Adventists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh-day_Adventist_Church "Seventh-day Adventist Church"). Charismatic groups such as [Jesus is Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_is_Lord "Jesus is Lord") (JIL), [Jesus Touch Fellowship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Touch_Fellowship?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jesus Touch Fellowship (page does not exist)") (JTF) and the [Life Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_Church_(Philippines)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Life Church (Philippines) (page does not exist)") (formerly known at the Life Renewal Center).

The [Members Church of God International (MCGI)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Members_Church_of_God_International "Members Church of God International") popularly called [Ang Dating Daan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Dating_Daan "Ang Dating Daan") established four church districts namely Calamian (Consisting of island municipalities in the North), Central (Consisting of Puerto Princesa City), North (Consisting of Northern municipalities) & South (Consisting of Southern municipalities) which signifies strong membership in the province.

Other Christian denominations including the indigenous [Iglesia ni Cristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iglesia_ni_Cristo "Iglesia ni Cristo") has many local congregations in the province established three Ecclesiastical District (Calamian, Palawan North, and Palawan South) each town has a barangay chapels signifies the existence of INC Faith, 2-3% of the entire province belongs to INC. The [United Church of Christ in the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Church_of_Christ_in_the_Philippines "United Church of Christ in the Philippines") or (UCCP), the [Jesus Miracle Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Miracle_Crusade "Jesus Miracle Crusade"), the [Pentecostal Missionary Church of Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentecostal_Missionary_Church_of_Christ?action=edit&redlink=1 "Pentecostal Missionary Church of Christ (page does not exist)") or PMCC (4th Watch) as well as the [Iglesia Filipina Independiente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iglesia_Filipina_Independiente "Iglesia Filipina Independiente") ([Philippine Independent Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Independent_Church "Philippine Independent Church") or Aglipayan Church) which is standing as one diocese (The Diocese of Palawan). [The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints "The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints") has a growing membership in the island province. [Jehovah's Witnesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jehovah's_Witnesses "Jehovah's Witnesses") have an active membership of 181,236 in the Philippines as of 2012. Special pioneers from the Witnesses have been preaching to prisoners at the [Iwahig Prison and Penal Farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iwahig_Prison_and_Penal_Farm "Iwahig Prison and Penal Farm") in Palawan, and were permitted to build a small Kingdom Hall right on the premises.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-77)

Around 75,000 to 100,000 Palawan residents (10% to 13%) identify as Muslims, these being mostly the native [Molbog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molbog_people "Molbog people") and [Palawano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawano_people "Palawano people") who are majority in [Balabac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balabac "Balabac") and [Bataraza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bataraza "Bataraza"), also significant in [Rizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rizal,_Palawan "Rizal, Palawan") and [Brooke's Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooke's_Point "Brooke's Point"), of the southern part of the island. Large numbers of [Jama Mapun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jama_Mapun "Jama Mapun") ([Mapun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mapun "Mapun") Island) and [Tausug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tausug_people "Tausug people") ([Sulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulu "Sulu")) migrants have also settled in southern Palawan, as well as a smaller number of [Sama Pangutaran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sama_people "Sama people") ([Tawi-Tawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tawi-Tawi "Tawi-Tawi")), [Maranao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maranao_people "Maranao people") ([Lanao del Sur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lanao_del_Sur "Lanao del Sur")), and [Yakan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakan_people "Yakan people") ([Basilan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilan "Basilan")). Maranao traders are more widely scattered throughout urban centers in Palawan, while the Yakan are mostly centered in the Rio Tuba area of Bataraza.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-nsohousing-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-Eder-79)

There are 52 languages and dialects in the province, with [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language "Tagalog language") being spoken by more than 50 percent of the people. Languages native to the islands are [Cuyonon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyonon "Cuyonon") (26.27 percent) and [Palawano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawano_language "Palawano language") (4.0 percent). [Kinaray-a](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinaray-a_language "Kinaray-a language") is also present in Palawan, spoken by 19 percent of inhabitants. Before mass immigration to Palawan by various groups of people from Southern Tagalog, Ilocandia, Central Luzon, and Panay, Cuyonon was an established [lingua franca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingua_franca "Lingua franca") amongst many of Palawan's native peoples, including the Agutaynen, Cagayanen, Tagbanua, Palawan, and others. The usage of Cuyonon significantly dropped during 1990s and the approach of the new millennium, being replaced by the now-majority Tagalog language, the reason for making Palawan part of Southern Tagalog.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-82) Tagalog may be usually spoken with [Batangas dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batangas_Tagalog "Batangas Tagalog") due to its geographical contact with [Batangas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batangas "Batangas") and Mindoro and Batangueño residents in the island. In Barangay Panitian, [Quezon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quezon,_Palawan "Quezon, Palawan"), Palawan, [Sambal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sambal_language "Sambal language") language is spoken by ethnic [Sambals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sambal_people "Sambal people"), who came from northern Zambales during the 1950s. In the south of Palawan during the occupation of the Sulu Sultanate, Tausug was a lingua franca amongst the minority Islamified ethnic groups, i.e., the Molbog, the Tausug (a non-native ethnic group), the Muslim Palaw'an, and the migratory Sama. By the 19th century, Cuyonon had replaced Tausug as a lingua franca. Many local Muslims and barter traders can also speak [Sabah Malay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabah_Malay "Sabah Malay").

English is spoken by a majority of the younger (age 20–39) population of [Puerto Princesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Princesa "Puerto Princesa"). It is spoken by a minority in every other area of the province.

Palawan's economy is basically agricultural. The three major crops are [palay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palay "Palay"), [corn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize "Maize") and [coconut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut "Coconut"). Mineral resources include [nickel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickel "Nickel"), [copper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copper "Copper"), [manganese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manganese "Manganese"), and [chromite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromite "Chromite"). Logging is also a major industry. Palawan has one of the richest fishing grounds in the country. About 45% of Manila's supply of fish comes from here. Having natural gas reserves of approximately 30,000 trillion cubic feet, the province is the only [oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil "Oil")-producing province in the country.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-pal_home-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-moscom2-93) In addition, [tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism "Tourism") is also a thriving sector, having received 1.8 million tourists in 2018, a 21% year-over-year increase from 2017.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-94)

Once considered the world's largest pearl, the 240 millimeters (9.4 in) diameter [Pearl of Lao Tzu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_of_Lao_Tzu "Pearl of Lao Tzu"), was found off Palawan in 1934.

The economic and agricultural business growth of province is at 20% per annum.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-moscom2-93) Coconut, sugar, rice, lumber, and livestock are produced here.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-encarta-11)

Unlike most of the Philippines, Palawan is [biogeographically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biogeography "Biogeography") part of [Sundaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundaland "Sundaland"), with a fauna and flora related to that found in [Borneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo "Borneo").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-95)

Palawan had 700,000 hectares (1,700,000 acres) of forests as of 2010[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-96) and has been called the Philippines' "last biodiversity frontier."[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-97)

Among the many [endemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemism "Endemism") species are the [Palawan peacock-pheasant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_peacock-pheasant "Palawan peacock-pheasant"), [Philippine mouse-deer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_mouse-deer "Philippine mouse-deer"), [Philippine pangolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_pangolin "Philippine pangolin"), [Palawan bearded pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_bearded_pig "Palawan bearded pig"), and [Palawan birdwing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_birdwing "Palawan birdwing"). In the forests and grasslands, the air resonates with the songs of more than 200 kinds of birds. Over 600 species of butterflies flutter around the mountains and fields of Palawan, attracted to some 1500 hosts plants found here. [Endangered sea turtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_sea_turtles "Endangered sea turtles") nest on white sand beaches.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-pal-98)[Sea turtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_turtles "Sea turtles") usually go to the nutrient-rich coastal waters of Palawan to rest and look for food. [Dugong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dugong "Dugong") numbers have fallen seriously, although Palawan still has a larger population than any other part of the country,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-99) and organizations such as [Community Centred Conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_Centred_Conservation?action=edit&redlink=1 "Community Centred Conservation (page does not exist)") (C3) are working to end the unsustainable use of marine resources in Palawan and in Philippines.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-100)

Total forest cover is about 56 percent of the total land area of the province while [mangrove forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangrove_forest "Mangrove forest") accounts for 3.35 percent based on the 1998 Landsat imagery. [Grasslands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasslands "Grasslands") dwindled from 19 percent in 1992 to 12.40 percent in 1998. This is an indication of improving soil condition as deteriorating soil is normally invaded by grass species. Brushlands increased to 25 percent of the total land area. Sprawled beneath the seas are nearly 11,000 square kilometers of [coral reefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_reefs "Coral reefs"), representing more than 35% of the country's coral reefs.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-pal-98)

Palawan, the only Philippine island cited, is rated by the _[Condé Nast Traveler Readers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cond%C3%A9\_Nast "Condé Nast")_ as the most beautiful island in the world and is also rated by the _[National Geographic Traveler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Geographic\_Traveler "National Geographic Traveler")_ magazine as the best island destination in [East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Asia "East Asia") and [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") region in 2007, and the equal 27th best island in the world having "incredibly beautiful natural seascapes and landscapes. One of the most biodiverse (terrestrial and marine) islands in the Philippines. The island has had a Biosphere Reserve status since the early 1990s, showing local interest for conservation and sustainable development".[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-102)

The province was also categorized as "doing well" in the 4th Destination Scorecard survey conducted by the [National Geographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Geographic_Society "National Geographic Society") Center for Sustainable Destinations, and _[Conde Nast Traveler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conde\_Nast\_Traveler "Conde Nast Traveler")_ magazine voted its beaches, [coves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cove "Cove") and [islets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islet "Islet") as the tourist destination with the best beaches in Asia.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-mst01-103) Renowned underwater explorer [Jacques Cousteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Cousteau "Jacques Cousteau") has described the province as having one of the most beautiful seascapes in the world.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan#cite_note-pal-98)
